text: I've been to this spa several times and there are some aspects of it that are wonderful and others that are truly bad. - Treatments: Nails: Pedicures have been OK to Good, but not spectacular. Good enough that if everything else was stellar, I'd come back, but nothing to write home about. The polish they use at this spa (Spa Ritual, I believe it is called), tends to chip before other pedicures I've had. The pedicures are done in a vibrating sound chair with a pedispa. I personally prefer a lounge chair and a basin of some sort because it is cleaner and less "neighborhood" spa like. Most spas I've been to have a more unique and posh feel when you're paying that much for a pedicure. This is a bit of a step up from that, but not by much. The massage and pampering part has been the same as getting your tootsies done down the street at Lucky Nail. Massage: I've had a regular massage here and a prenatal massage. Both times my therapist was pretty chatty and I didn't feel that they'd truly been trained in upscale spa etiquette. This wouldn't be as big of a deal, but when I'm paying through the nose, I expect a professional experience. Vichy Shower: I had the VIchy experience here and it was ok, though I did feel that my therapist was winging it and not fully trained. I would not do this treatment again ever. I just felt like I was being drowned in a shower with a wet towel over my head while I was lying down. Two thumbs down. I'm not sure that this is supposed to be relaxing, but it was truly awful. Spa amenities/Wet areas: This is where this spa does shine actually. I love the Caldarium area with the pool, hot and cold plunge and the vibrating massage loungers. I've been to this spa about 4 or 5 times, and usually one or two of the 5 loungers are broken, but you can usually still find one to sit in at some point if you want. The women's locker room has it's own sauna/steam/hot tub/cold plunge which is nice, and they have the normal snacks/water/juice expected in a spa. Front desk area/policies: This is where they lost a lot of stars. Expect to be treated like you just showed up at Supercuts or something. Twice I was treating a friend and didn't want or need them to know how much it cost and yet the front desk clerk talks loud enough that people can here her all the way to the door of the spa. I said twice, "I'm paying and treating her". Then she put the amount in front of my guest to sign. I repeated, that I was treating as a gift and that she didn't need to know the amount her treatment is. The online information also said that there wasn't gratuity included, yet I was charged a gratuity. I was going to tip anyway, but I want to tip what I want to tip. That's what a gratuity is. It's a tip for a job well done. If it is part of the charge, you should just charge more for the service. I find it to be an underhanded way to suck people dry and for this reason alone, I will not be back to this spa again. Between that and the front desk person being very unprofessional and nearly rude, I just had my fill. I did try several times to make this spa work for me, but it always leaves a bad taste in my mouth. If I am spending a couple hundred bucks somewhere to have a relaxing experience, I'd be foolish to repeat going somewhere that didn't work for me. It's such a shame though, I know they put a lot of effort into the renovation, the treatments aren't bad, and this place had so much promise. If you are looking for me, I'll be at the Atlantis spa.

The food there is amazing, though definitely not cheap. The bartenders and servers are trained and tested in their wine and fine whiskey knowledge so you can trust them select a good match for you. The layout and design of Ombi is very sleek and trendy, but not in an obnoxious Gulch-y way. A great time to check it out is when they do a wine or food tasting so make sure to check their calendar. Another good time is at the (monthly?) Forward parties where they offer great drink specials like $6 name your gin/vodka martinis.

text: Devon is just the right kind of seafood restaurant. Lively and clean, busy and bright. You see eating seafood, especially shellfish is a brisk and boisterous affair. You gotta get your fingers into it. Devon is elegant but still brisk. The waitstaff is handsome and professional, and the food is first rate. If you can get a seat, get ready for feast size platters cooked to perfection. The wine list is tremendous, and although I'm not a huge wine fanatic, I know a good Riesling when I taste one, and a good Riesling is de rigeur if you're doing serious shellfish. Well, that's how my mama raised me. The main dining room is in a clever cave-like section that looks rather like a refurbished subway tunnel. That's a good thing, it's very tastefully done and it adds to just the right atmosphere of fun, even though this is a fairly classy joint. Right on Rittenhouse Square, Devon is in the high zoot neighborhood and last time I went by there was a convertible Aston-Martin DB9 parked out front. (Yes it had paddle shifters). So scrub your face and bring your wallet, and your appetite. Now as far as I'm concerned there are just a few signature dishes that tell me how good a seafood restaurant is. The first (and the only one I tried here) is the Lobster Bisque. Devon's gets four stars, and so does the restaurant.

It might have tasted better if the smothered it in enough pizza sauce, cheese and onions, but there sure wasn't enough of any of those! text: Doobie's is BY FAR my absolute favorite bar in Philadelphia. I'm there at least once a week with my co-workers and honestly don't plan on changing that trend. I really don't have anything to complain about. I probably should start off by saying that Doobie's is a dive. It's dark, kitschy, has Christmas lights up year-round, and the bathroom doors are notorious for lots of graffiti (Check out the KCL = 3 Lushkateers tag in the ladies bathroom...that's right, I did that). But honestly, it's the bar that I always hoped I'd find. I walk in there and I'm guarenteed to know or recognize at least 3 people because everyone there is so friendly. The wait staff is also really nice and a few of them I've come to consider friends as opposed to just people I see out. By the way, check out the box of board games they keep by the back door. It contains the majority of games from you childhood and, while that may not sound fun to some, drunken games of Scrabble or Life are basically the best 45 minutes to an hour spent. The jukebox is also pretty good. It's one of those rare jukes that doesn't download the music from the internet and contains gems such as The Pixies, Tom Waites, and Ella Fitzgerald. In terms of food and beverages, it's on par. The really nice thing about Doobie's is that they definitely cater to vegetarians. I was honestly surprised to see the amount of vegan food they serve on both their regular menu and their specials menu. Some of it is kind of bland, but when you're hammered and the drunchies kick in then it's exactly what you need. They also have a pretty decent beer selection and offer pitchers, something that can be rare these days. They won't empty your wallet but be warned - it's cash only. I highly recommend this place to everyone. It may not look like much at first but I promise you that it's great. Also - if you're there Sunday nights then come say hi. I'm the huge nerd playing Scrabble :D

text: My soon to be Mother and Father in-law took me to Amelia's Tea & Holly for my birthday. I'm so happy there's a nice little tea room so close by! My fiancé and I used to travel to Cape May to Twinings' Tea Room for this sort of experience, but Amelia's is a place we can visit a bit more often. The tea room is in a nice Victorian off Main Street in Mullica Hill, NJ. Upon entering, there is a little shop selling all things tea. Lots of ceramics, tea packs, and decorations are available for purchase. Past the shop is the restaurant which is decorated to the hilt with old pictures, vintage clothing, hats of all sorts on the walls, and trinkets galore! The table settings were all unique -- no two items were the same. We all enjoyed the Queen's Tea which includes your choice of tea, assorted tea sandwiches, a scone, quiche, fruit, soup, and lots of sweets. During our visit, the soup was a tomato bisque which was delicious and rich with flavor. This was my favorite part of the meal. The sandwiches were all very good as well. There were so many sweets! I packed them up in a to go box because there was no way I could (or should) have eaten them all! My fiancé will enjoy those later tonight, I'm sure! The service was good although side plates, clotted cream and jam were forgotten when our food was presented. The server was close by so it wasn't long before we got her attention and she returned with the forgotten items. I had a lovely time and will definitely be returning. Great for that tea room experience. I recommend it.

text: The only thing Mexican about Los Caballitos is the name. Commonly referred to as just "The Cantina." The food leaves a lot to be desired. I suspect there isn't one actual mexican person involved in this establishment. If you're looking for actual Mexican food, go across the street to El Zarape. The drink selection isn't bad. They offer various tequila flights ranging from top shelf to low end. The margaritas and mojitos are available in some interesting flavors, but they feel a little over priced, but their happy hour lasts until 7pm which cuts the price of the margs in half. text: Fiesta is the time of year that most of the locals I know leave town, (myself especially)! It's loud, it's crowded with tourists, drunks, frat-boys, scantily to obscenely clad young girls and gang-bangers from Oxnard. The bars all charge a high cover fee in order to maximize their Fiesta time income. Even worse than this, the city brings in police forces from all over the state to stand around and eye you under the glare of the bright Third Reich lighting that is also hauled in and installed for the whole occasion. LOUD mariachi bands everywhere and you can't escape the noise and the confetti from all those eggs. It's awful! --- it's messy, it's touristy and it SUCKS. --- Avoid at all costs!!! IF you are a local, then you know that there are a couple of redeeming qualities about Fiesta. For one, those tamales at Our Lady Of Guadalupe church rule. The El Mercado market that they set up in De La Guerra Plaza can be really fun when local bands like Spencer The Gardener are playing. Some of the food is pretty decent too. The Fiesta horse parade is cool. Family fun minus all the drunks that are home nursing thier hangovers from the night before. I especially like the firemen float. Most of all, though, I can totally recommend the Fiesta Bike Run. It takes place on the last day of the whole mess, (usually a Sunday). Bring your bike, some sunscreen, water and a fun attitude. It's total bike chaos, meeting at the dolphin fountain at Stearns Wharf and then proceeding up State st., fully and completely taking over the streets like Critical Mass. SO MUCH FUN! If you've ever been in something like this, you know how much fun it is. Horns honking, people hootin' and hollerin'. It's a total blast. Fun for the whole family and some good excersize too. Although they complain and threaten to every year, I hope they never succeed in shutting down the cruiser run.

text: I'll preface this review by saying the last time I ate here was 8 months ago, so some changes may have been made to improve the problems I encountered. The overall message I took from my meal there was that the staff at 275 Hill, from the servers to the kitchen staff, had absolutely no investment in my experience and could care less whether I enjoy my meal and my time there. Everything struck me as careless: our server was unpolished and unprofessional in her approach and presentation. She dumped a full plate of crumbs on me, and then dripped a drink on me, and dismissed both instances with a casual "Oops." When my friend ordered a drip coffee, she brought back an americano because their drip machine wasn't on or working. She told him "It's a shot of espresso with water. At the end of the meal, she gave us a bill that listed the owner's previous restaurant at the top of the receipt and "Open Item" for every single thing we ordered, making it impossible to verify if the tab was correct. It tasted like canned seafood that had been opened up and left in a refrigerator for weeks. All I could taste was the refrigerator. It was absolutely disgusting. My other friends' reactions (one of whom is a professional San Francisco chef) ranged from very disappointed to marginally satisfied. But even the ones who were marginally satisfied left with a bad taste in their mouth from the atrocious service. I came to 275 Hill wanting to embrace a new Reno restaurant. I had heard about the eclectic menu and was truly excited to try this place. My recommendation to the management would be to stop looking at their patrons as wallets, and start looking at them as guests. Take care of them, invest in their entire experience, and don't cut corners in your kitchen. If 275 Hill did this, I think they could fill their restaurant with happy return customers. text: I had to have a root canal done...I know what you're thinking, already. You think this review is biased based on my pain and my secret (not now!) fear of death by drowning in my own saliva during any dental procedure! Well, I wish it were...but unfortunately, it was just a bad experience. :( Let me break this down into a few different aspects here: The Actual Procedure The procedure was mostly wonderful. The dentist I had drew me a picture on paper and on my x-ray to show me an overview what he was going to do (he did leave out the exact details such as the scary rubber dam contraption - had NO idea that was coming!), which was nice because I was nervous. He also answered several questions I had, one of which was "How long will this take?!" to which he replied, "30 to 45 minutes." I kept that number in my head - we'll revisit it later... Anyway, back to procedure. I barely felt him give me the numbing shots, at all. He was very good at that. I hated the rubber dam they put in my mouth but it's part of the process so can't blame them for that. I do wish, however, that they would've paid more attention to my excessive drooling (I did let them know ahead of time that I tend to produce a LOT of saliva!...Seriously!) and also that they would've told me exactly what they were doing as they were doing it instead of talking over the top of me about what political radio shows they are currently listening to and whether or not peaches were left in someone's car. Sadly, I got screwed, and screwed GOOD when I was there (for my first tattoo, sadly). First off, after talking to the girl at the counter and discussing what I wanted (sun and moon off an album cover) and who I wanted to do it, I was told that if I would come back in an hour I could get it done that day. Great, right? When I returned, the person I assumed was the artist I'd requested came up and showed me the sketch of my tattoo. It looked enough like the original, just an outline without much detail. This was my first tattoo, so I foolishly thought that the detail wasn't necessary for the stencil and he'd just work off the original image. WRONG. You can see what I ended up with. It's since been covered up. With something bigger, fancier, and also THE SAME PRICE as the first one. Months later, I visited the Electric Ladyland website and discovered that the person that did this tattoo was NOT the artist I had picked (I knew only his name, not what he looked like). I've only given the place two stars because it was clean, the guy that did my tattoo did explain everything and was actually very nice (I believe his name may have been PJ, and he relocated after Katrina). My boyfriend at the time got a custom tattoo from the same place (different artist) and his turned out really well. The artist that covered up this tattoo for me was pretty surprised when he found out where it came from. This happened in 2005, so I wouldn't necessarily dissuade anyone from going there, as long as they KNOW who their chosen artist is and make sure that they GET that artist.

The one serious complaint I had with this place is the fee for the golf course. A round of golf - $150. They gave us a discount and let us play for $120. text: Maggianos is an Italian chain restaurant, and if you enjoy Italian-American food or if you just like getting a lot of food for your money, then you'll like Maggianos. The restaurant interior is very classy. White tablecloths, waiters dressed in black slacks and long-sleeved collared shirts, etc. It's a little nicer than, say, an Olive Garden or Buca di Beppo. It's definitely not tacky. It's got the kind of look that makes you feel like you might have to dress up a little, but it's not like they're not going to seat you if you're wearing a t-shirt and jeans, though most patrons will be a little dressy. There are your typical appetizers; calamari, fried zucchini, bruschetta and crostini, and all are made well. I usually get the zucchini when I'm there, and it is always crisp, never greasy. The pasta portions are huge for the cost, and the menu offers "classic pastas" that are "buy one, take one home". Basically, they bring you out your dinner choice, and your take home choice is boxed up and given to you before you leave. It's a good way to get tomorrow's lunch for work while you're eating tonight's dinner. Aside from the pasta, the entrees are good, but a little more expensive, and you might not get as full as you would eating the pasta dishes. Still, everything I've ever ordered here has been good, I've never been disappointed with anything I've ordered. Favorite for sure is the Rigatoni D, which is rigatoni tossed with button mushrooms and chicken in a asiago cream sauce. Very good. Lasagna is also very good. I can't speak too much about their various desserts, because I only ever get tiramisu if I do order dessert. Sorry, I can't help you out more, but I'm just a sucker for tiramisu. On nights where I just don't feel like cooking, and I want Italian, but don't feel like going to a really high end place , Maggianos is always a reliable standby. I prefer it to all other Italian chains in Nashville, I always feel like I got a lot for the money, and the food has never disappointed. Word of advice, though, DEFINITELY get reservations if you plan on being there anytime after 6 on Thursdays through Saturdays. The restaurant fills up really quickly, and for obvious reasons. Also, they advertise a lot for large groups, catering, etc. I can't speak for how their catering is, but they do offer it, in case you're curious.

text: Always on Point - Great Place! Derek's is one of my go-to restaurants. I'm actually even going today! I go at least once a month whether it's for drinks and small plates or a full-fledged dinner. Dinner at Derek's is amazing. So is the brunch with unlimited mimosas! Wow! I love that you can cut down on the cost of dinner by bringing your own wine, but it's also great that they have such a good selection of both specialty cocktails and wines available. Their soup is one of my favorite things there. Their soup of the day tends to be my favorite - including butternut squash soup and portabella mushroom. Their goat cheese salad is delicious and I find that I crave it for days after my visit. The filet is amazing as is the braised pork shoulder and roasted duck breast. The combination of grits and hominy with the pork is a refreshing twist and makes this one of my boyfriend's favorite meals ever. The steak and mushroom salad is always a hit, as are the shrimp and crab spring rolls - delicious dipping sauce. Dessert is also good. It's not the absolute best bread pudding I've ever had (Stone Rose in Conshohocken), but it was pretty good with a great texture. The creme brulee, however, was perfect! It passed my "tock-tock test," that I learned from a chef in London. Tap your spoon on top of the creme brulee and listen for a "tock-tock" sound to see if it was caramelized properly and is crisp. It always is AND it's made with real vanilla bean, which I can see in the creme. I haven't found a better creme brulee in Philly yet. If you haven't been to Derek's yet - GO! The ambiance is fantastic, the bar area is lush and inviting and the food is to die for. This is by far one of my favorite Philadelphia restaurants!

text: I have finally experienced the awesomeness that is Xochitl. Reluctantly, after several seasons of passing up on Restaurant Week, I decided to give the promotion another shot. Xochitl has made me a believer again. My friend and I arrived slightly early for our 7 p.m. resie but we were escorted to a table immediately. Our water glasses were filled and bread was dropped off with two buttery spreads. Our server, whose name escapes me, was wonderful throughout the experience. When she asked to take our drink order and I handed over the recipe for a "Skinnygirl Margarita," she didn't bat an eye although she did let me know that their regular margaritas are made only with tequila, fresh lime juice and a little bit of simple syrup. No sour mix, no triple sec, no hidden agendas; just honest ingredients, served over ice, with a rim of salt. I ended up taking her word for it. (For the record, one Skinnygirl plus two positively delicious Xochitl margs equals three sheets to the wind, minus any trace of a stomachache, which I almost always get when I drink margaritas anywhere else. Hallelujah!) The food was glorious. For our first course, we both chose the tortilla soup. Large bowls containing cubes of cheese, slices of avocado, tortilla strips and dried peppers were presented to both of us. The broth was poured on top, tableside. I really enjoyed this dish, although my friend and I agreed that the dried peppers had a curious taste. She didn't like them, I was intrigued by them. Next, we both ordered the octopus, mackerel and shrimp ceviche trio. Each was served atop a little fried tortilla round. I have been daydreaming about the octopus ceviche since I awoke this morning. It was easily the most tender, well flavored octopus I have had (sorry, Mr. Garces). For my entrée, I chose the squid hot pot, which was another win. When the lid was removed from the pot, tender rings of squid in a spicy tomato sauce appeared before us. I have to say, the dramatic presentations really made the dining experience special. The woman seated next to me ordered a stuffed pepper that was so beautiful it could have easily been pictured in a food magazine. Meanwhile, at our table, my friend had food envy as she was experiencing mixed feelings about her skirt steak (which I thought was good, although it was served lukewarm). For dessert, my friend had the churros, which came with three dipping sauces. One of my favorite things in life is the right to choose several condiments to go with a meal and this presentation was right up my alley. Fortunately, I had my own dessert to tackle; an appropriately sized mini chocolate soufflé with a mini scoop of cajeta ice cream alongside. Perfection. Our experience last night wasn't just great by Restaurant Week standards; it was great by any night's standards. What a truly fantastic meal. When our bill was dropped, along with a plate of mini biscotti (delish, by the way), we were also each given a $10 card to use any time before November 31. My dining companion and I are already discussing what we will order on our return visit!

text: If you've ever walked down 3rd Street (towards Arch) then you've smelled the amazing aromas coming out of this spa...they're enough to make even a jaded city dweller stop in their tracks and breathe deep. Now just imagine how great it is to step inside and get treated to a massage, facial or any other treatment they offer. It's pretty darn awesome! I credit Terme Di Aroma as being the only place to give me a massage that made me fall asleep on the table - no small feat as I get lots of them but still find it really hard to relax. I highly recommend adding on the reflexology option to whatever service you're getting (your tootsies will thank you), as it just prolongs the magic. text: I wanted Sang Hing to be excellent and wanted to be really surprised by the food for a simple reason, I pass it on the way from work to home. Unfortunately the food was fairly standard chinese take out here in Delaware. The fried rice was cooked well without burnt or mushy grains, the pork was average. There was no thick crust to the char siu in the fried rice to enrich the flavor. It did however, have some flavor and was not mushy. The bean sprouts were crisp and the onions had some bite to it. The crispy orange chicken was cooked well, thicker breading but not overly doughy. The orange sauce was a bit thick and sweet, no brisk and bright orange flavor here. The staff was quick and friendly. This is more of a take out place given that the seating is very limited and small. Unfortunately the dishes were standard chinese takeout in Delaware, but well made. I have been disappointed in the americanized chinese take out that is available in Delaware. I am more so disappointed because I know from seeing the dishes that are made by the different restaurants that different dishes could be made very well. But Delaware seems to be happy with substandard versions of Americanized chinese takeout. The restaurants have to cater to what the community wants I guess. I am fine with eating here again as the food is well made, just not the quality of Chinese take out I am used to; but fairly standard in Delaware.
label: NEG

text: This is the closest bowling 'center' (you will find out in a minute why I'm using this term rather than alley) to my house and is right across the street from the new Nashville West shopping plaza on Charlotte Pike. If you're coming here expecting just a bowling alley you're in for a treat (or a shock depending on your personality). Its main function is yes, a bowling center, but it is also so much more than that. Strike and Spare is like a scaled down, less expensive, locally owned version of a Dave and Busters. They've got a large arcade area featuring many different games that cover all your bases. From DDR to shooting games to racing games, there's something for everyone. It doesn't stop there, however, Strike and Spare has bumper cars, a roller skating rink and even laser tag! Whether you have kids or just like acting like one, it's a great place to spend hours running around being ridiculous. I can't forget about their bowling though. They offer the largest number of lanes in town and it is practically impossible to come and not find a free lane. Their pricing is great you can pay per game or by the hour and they've got specials and deals pretty much every day of the week. They of course serve beer but for some reason not pitchers and their food is of the expected greasy quality (although their menu is a little more extensive than some bowling alleys). Because of its diverse selection of activities it is a popular place for birthday parties and get-togethers for all ages. The place is bright, cheery and clean which are typically things you don't associate with a bowling alley. The employees are helpful and you can't beat their location which is convenient to I-40 and just a 10 or so minute drive from downtown up Charlotte Pike.
label: POS

text: While I don't live in Tucson, this is one of my must-eat-at places when I visit. Their chicken melt is to die for! There is always live music of some sort and it's not that in your face loud mariachi, but good background music that you can enjoy. I've been here twice a year for about four years now and in my opinion, nothing has changed. The service is fantastic, the margaritas are strong, and the food is delish. text: Dental insurance in full effect: time to find a dentist. Dr. Pittman has a brand new office that is a kinda tricky to find, but it's seriously awesome. Whoever thought of this was a genius. The entire place has a very modern feel to it, and his staff are all super friendly. Dr. Pittman took time to show me the x-rays on the screen and explain what means what and explained his idea of running a dental office like a family. Which is better than any experience I have ever had. All in all, top of the line equipment, great staff, and a personable dentist who speaks English and not dental jargon make this place my new dental office. text: We found a dog and took it into the Humane Society. They told us that it would cost $35 to give the dog to them to find the owner. They also said if we decided to keep the dog they would take down all of the dog's information. They SAID this information would be in their computer and listed on a website called Found! (www.found-pets.org). They gave us a control # and told us to take photos of the dog and send them with the control # to the Found! website. We asked them to scan the dog for a microchip, the worker did a half-ass swipe of the dog and said there was no microchip. We went home, took photos and followed their instructions to inform the Found! website. I also posted a listing on Craigslist. The next day the owner, on a whim, checked Craigslist and called us. The owner was frantic and both her & the dog were happy with the reunion. The owner then told us how she called the Humane Society and check the Found! website several times on Sunday and Monday. She was told by the HS that no dog matching her dog's description was brought in and the listing on Found! was never put up. She also informed us that her dog was microchipped! Unfortunately my husband and I have had other several unacceptable experiences with the HS here in Tucson. I won't get into every experience we've had with their rude and incompetent staff, but this recent incident really put me over the edge! I would strongly encourage people who have lost or found a pet to use Craigslist instead of only relying on the HS/Found! faulty system. I truly hope that the HS can take this criticism to heart and make adjustments.

text: I've never been here to eat, only to drink and party. I like that there's a good amount of space and you can approach the bar from two sides. They keep people's credit cards with a piece of paper attached to it with a paper clip. Everything is calculated manually. I had to look through all the cards on the counter to tell them which one was mine. At the end of the night, I had mysteriously accumulated a $91 bill - I had noticed that someone else had the same exact credit card as me. text: I love doing my grocery shopping at Trader Joe's. They always have a good selection of yummy food that you wouldn't find in other grocery stores. Another plus is that you don't have to pay ghastly prices for these non-standard treats. They also have a good return policy, which I have yet to use. Produce is wrapped in set quantities, which keeps it in better shape, (but is a bit wasteful.) They offer up a selection of lactose-free products (aka soy based) and gluten-free products, so if you have special dietery needs, its a nice place to shop. They also have a good variety of organic foods and products if that floats your boat. If you're looking for baking basics, I would try a different store. Sometimes it's hard to find plain ol' flour, baking soda, etc. The wine selection is good, and if you want cheap they have their 2 buck chuck - yup bottles of Charles Shaw wine sell for $2. At this location the delivery truck comes around 7 pm, making the parking lot difficult to navigate. On the bright side, there usually aren't as many people shopping at this time.

text: This is my 2nd trip to the Bon-Aire. I was introduced last year by my wife who has come here since she was a little girl. Admittedly, I probably wouldn't stay here if I drove in & needed to decide on a place by looks as there are some nicer-looking high-rise places to stay. But if you want to run to your room quickly from the beach or pool without taking an elevator to a double-digit floor, then this is the place. Stay here once & you'll want to return. The 2 pools are GREAT (warm enough to get in, but cool enough to be refreshing) Sandbar Bill's is a great grill with great food. Its on-site yet open to anyone on the beach. The hotel is literally ON THE BEACH. You can walk out from the back patio onto the beach & another short jaunt & you'll be standing in the Gulf of Mexico. This hotel caters to all types of travelers. They have a number of different room styles to accommodate families, retirees, spring breakers, etc. Another positive to this hotel is its location to other needs! Walgreens across the street & Publix within walking distance. If you visit St Pete Beach, you should stay at the Bon-Aire!

text: I grew up in West Chester, just outside Philly. Whenever we made the journey into the city, it was no question that a stop to Geno's and Italiano's (if in the appropriate season) were on the day's agenda. We'd pull up to the parking spaces in front, always decorated with American flags. This is the type of family shop where the owners know you by name and order. My dad? Brian, large pineapple. My brother? Patrick, large vanilla. As for me? Well, I would always stare in awe of the huge list of available flavors, but in the end I was usually Kathryn, small watermelon. As a child, I was always so amazed that mine had real chunks of watermelon. After mining through his Italian ice my Dad would give me some his chunks of golden pineapple, too. Returning here always reignites that childish excitement inside me. Even now I take a while to browse the long list of offered flavors, but usually wind up as Kat, medium mint chocolate chip and chocolate ice gelati. If you want water ice, go to Rita's. If you want Italian Ice and the original Gelati, come to Italiano's. You won't regret it.

One waitstaff for the entire restaurant doesn't seem to be enough. There were long wait for food and service, which I suspect there's only one staff in the kitchen as well. The pizza was also really good, they had a pesto/tomato/mushroom one that had a really nice, chewy crust and good flavor to it. For the amount and quality of food my friends and I ate, I can't believe they can make money on this buffet. text: Summer is almost over and 'tis now the season of the local festival! If you're looking for something a little different in the way of a weekend outing, consider the St. Joan of Arc Catholic Church French Market. Now in its 19th year, this festival is consistently one of the best and biggest in Indy and is held each year on the second Saturday after Labor Day. This event is a food, arts and crafts and live entertainment bonanza that, as the name implies, revolves around a French theme. Admission is free, too, so you really can't go wrong here. Some of the highlights of the French Market include a bevy of French edibles such as ratatouille, beignets, quiche, moules and eclairs; a raffle with some great prizes; a full schedule of live bands and of course, dozens of vendor booths with a wide array of art and handcrafted items. It's true that the food isn't exactly cheap at this event, but then festival food never is....and this menu is at least a step above the standard "dipped and fried" variety. If the weather is decent, expect this event to be packed, especially as dusk draws near. This is when the courtyard area in front of the performance stage will begin to fill up like crazy as festival-goers settle in at a table with their food and wine to enjoy the bands. The ambiance really kicks it up a notch after dark, too, as multiple strings of lights criss-crossed above the tables in the courtyard lend an authentic French touch....with a little imagination, you may be able to find yourself in a open-air cafe tucked away on a little side street in oldtown Nice.

text: Rae's is without question the best sandwich shop in Downtown Nashville and my vote for the best in the whole city. All of the sandwiches are fresh and made to order. Their specialty is hot sandwiches warmed up on cast iron skillets in a hot oven. Some of the best examples of this are their Monte Cristo (turkey, ham, bacon and melted cheese sauce), the Italian Romeo (Italian breast of chicken, artichoke hearts, and sundried tomatoes with melted provo), and the sinfully good Black and Bleu (sliced beef tenderlion with spicy cajun mayo and bleu cheese crumbles.) I have had each of these multiple times and am never, ever disappointed. In fact I would not hesitate to recommend any sandwich on their entire menu even the vegetarian ones which focus on roasted mushrooms and the previously mentioned artichoke hearts. One quick tip if you do not have a huge appetite is to order a half sandwich. Still plenty of food and you will not be tempted to eat the whole thing (believe me you will not want to stop.) In addition to fantastic sandwiches they also have a rotating selection of soups and excellent salads, oh and don't forget the fresh brownies. The staff is always friendly and will get to know your name if you go often enough. The only downsides is that it can get very crowded during the lunch rush and it is in an out of the way location if you do not work in the downtown area. It is also only open for lunch but if you order a full sized sandwich you could probably have enough left over for dinner. I say probably because I have yet to have enough discipline to stop eating one of their sandwiches. Make a special trip or meet a friend downtown, it will be worth it.

text: Oh so much disappointment! I drive by Elle everyday on my way to work meaning I pass this building twice a day upto 7 days week sometimes. text: In the past I've used capital grille as a jumping off point for other restaurants. Come here, have a decent cocktail, then head out. For a change, my guest and I decided to have lunch here yesterday. The host was not to be found, but Ralph, the pleasant bartender, waved us in and had our drink orders in process in no time. We glanced at the menu, but decided to stay when he described the scallop special. This was three large 'lion's paw' scallops, served of a toasted brioche bun, lightly sauced and complimented with fresh grape and mini heirloom tomatoes. My guest and I exchanged glances knowing one of us was going to order this. I blinked first, so he won out. I had the Wagyu carpaccio as a consolation prize. At $15, the carpaccio was nice. It was served with a huge mountain of endive, large curls of aged provolone, and 1/2 a lemon to squeeze as desired. I shoveled a mouthful of greens in only to find yowza! they were dressed with a pepper/horseradish dressing that really had a kick. Now, had this been prime Kobe, I would have been very unhappy to have this much intensity taking away from the base taste of my beef. No worries there. The 'Wagyu' beef was far from top notch. In fact, as we looked at the beef we could see that what had happen was the usual poor prep. The beef had been frozen so the could cut it paper thin. This breaks down the meat a bit and causes it to rip to shreds (or simply turn to mush) when you disturb it. Worse, after this was cut the plate was left out, sans salad, waiting for little ole me to order it. While it waited, the beef air dried to literal dried beef. Luckily the dressing and a liberal squirt of lemon reconstituted it well. Overall, I did really like this dish, but don't be passing off JRZY heffer as Kobe. Call it what it is, a lovely beef carpaccio, and move along. Yes, I would order it again, for $15 it was a well priced dish, and it tasted good. The scallops were a knockout. One of the few places where the scallops were perfectly cooked, they were then lightly seasoned with garlic and a light drizzle of olive oil. Hardly the size of a Lion paw, they were good size nonetheless. The brioche went perfectly, it's roasted eggy richness soaking up all the juices of the scallops and tomatoes as you munched along. The tomatoes were a lovely mix of small grape, tiny yellow pear, and quartered purple russians. A bit heavy on the garlic, the dish overall was exceptional and for $17, a win in our book. A side note on our bartender. He was polite, meticulous, there when you needed him and not when you didn't. He also understood that if you enjoy a dirty martini on the very dirty side, you tend to have an 'overage' after you pour, and rather than shoot it down the sink like some places do, he didn't. text: Good, bad, both... I went here for the first time about 2 years ago while in town and ended up eating here 3 times (2 lunches and a dinner). I thought it was really really tasty. They had a great bread pudding, great sandwiches, great burgers, etc. The service was also really quick and servers were nice. I just went back to Nashville for a car show and convinced my parents to go for dinner one night. Apparently they changed chefs or the chef changed menu items or something, didn't really know exactly what the server said. We started out with the spinach artichoke dip which wasn't horrible, but it was really runny. For our dinner, we ordered pork chop, brie salad, and chicken sandwich. I had the sandwich and I ordered a side of the spicy chipotle mayo with it. They did not lie about the spicy part of it!!! It was good, but my mouth was on fire while I was eating it. The sandwich tasted like a chicken sandwich that you would order from any restaurant, nothing special about it, but no complaints either. The pork chop was full of fat, and nowhere near the cost. The salad had really runny dressing and when asked for a side of dressing (twice), it never came. Every time we had an issue that the server knew about, he disappeared and didn't reappear until the problem was fixed which was fine except that he would disappear for 10 minutes at a time while everyone's drinks would be empty (and with that spicy chipotle mayo, you need a full glass at all times). At this point, my parents had no clue why I told them we had to go there, but we stayed for dessert because my mom loves bread pudding when it has chocolate chips instead of raisins, which they have. We also ordered carrot cake and chocolate cake. The description of the chocolate cake said something about it being chocolate cake with chocolate icing. When I got my "chocolate cake", it was not cake, it was mousse. I never would have ordered it had I known that. I took a bite thinking maybe it had cake somewhere, but it didn't, it was just mousse. The carrot cake was small and round and 90 percent frosting. There was approximately 2 spoon fulls of actual carrot cake hidden under tons of frosting. When the server came back and saw that I only took one bite of the chocolate "cake", he said yeah, our chef changed it today (thanks for the warning), but I will take it back since you didn't like it. This was very nice considering that I didn't even ask him to do that, but he never offered me another dessert, just took it back. It is fine, I didn't need the calories anyways. Our bill was around 100 bucks for 1 appetizer, 3 meals, and 2 desserts. Overall this 2nd experience was nowhere near as good as the first, but the bread pudding is still delicious so I would maybe go back for just that. They are getting ready to do a major remodel so hopefully after that they will work on getting their food back to being good!

text: Last night I partook in the lamb dinner (to be read, "epic lamb feast"). I loved it. So much. The salad is sort of like cole slaw, which was sort of weird but, well heck, I like cole slaw and this was pretty good cole slaw. Whatever! The main course is an enormous plate with an assortment of lamb pieces on one side, and some of the tastiest potatoes on the other side that you'll have anywhere. By the time you're finished, you either need a box or you are nearly paralyzed. I was nearly paralyzed. But one of my friends -- the only other person in my party to finish his plate, bless his soul -- raised the stakes: he asked for the dessert menu! Now, in case you haven't picked this up yet, I was flippin' stuffed, and so was he. But those desserts sounded GOOD! There were five of us, and we split a piece of baklava, a Bosnian Delight (basically a cookie cake thing soaked in sweet syrup with crushed nuts on the bottom), and an order of Nutella crepes. My poor stomach...they were so delicious I couldn't help but dive headlong into the fray, and all three desserts were gone in minutes. For five people to feast heartily on lamb and three desserts at under $100 is pretty impressive. text: Wow, if this really is Indy's best Sushi, I may have to drive to Chicago more often. Came here last weekend with the wife and a couple friends. At times she seemed to be super attentive, and at other times she was no where to be found. Our hostess came by a few times and apologized for our lack of service. While usually we would be upset by this, we weren't in any kind of rush, and we were actually waiting for our friends to join, so it wasn't such a big deal. MENU- so this place is an "Asian Fusion" joint. I guess by Asian fusion they mean a bit of Japanese and mostly KOREAN. They had your typical katsu and bento boxes, but a majority of it was Korean (ie bi bim bop, ja keon [pa keon maybe?], etc...). They did have General Tso's chicken, so maybe that made them more of a "fusion" joint. Their sushi menu seemed pretty cool, though a good number of rolls had KRAB (imitation crab people). I understand it drives costs down, but you can tell the difference. FOOD-To start with, my wife and I tried the scallion and seafood pancake. For being deep fried, it was surprisingly light, and was pretty tasty. From there my wife ordered a spicy scallop roll and a crunch roll of some sort. I had the spicy seafood stir fry (scallops, shrimp, calamari, and oysters). My co-worker ordered the sushi sampler A or something, and his girlfriend got a chicken wrap of some sort. My co-worker and his girlfriend were not amazed by the food, but they thought it was decent. My wife and I on the other hand were a bit disappointed. Our spicy scallop roll was not what we had envisioned (cut up scallop on top of the roll), and her crunch roll lacked any kind of flavor, let alone crunch. My spicy seafood was MOSTLY vegetables, and the seafood that was there was mostly calamari. I had 2 shrimp, 2 (small) scallop and I think 2 oysters. Pretty disappointing. OVERALL- Even though I had read all the hype, I withered my expectations a bit, knowing this might not be that good. Sadly, my withered expectations weren't even met. I may give this place another try, but not in the near future. Chuck Norris rating- donkey kick

text: My visiting daughter and family wanted to try some "famous cheesesteaks", so off we went to the two big rivals, right across the street from each other. Geno's was right there, so we asked them and they slipped her into the back and left her piddle. Now we get to friendliness, cleanliness and decor. Pat's is old and dirty and has not spent one dime of their profits to stand out in these three fields. Geno's on the other hand has put a lot into these areas. Now for the cheesesteaks: Even though we were all headed to Pat's, my daughter and I were so impressed with Geno's that we ordered our steak and fries there. The other 5 in our party stayed at Pat's. text: Founded by a grieving father who could not find his young daughters grave in a church graveyard in Old City, Laurel Hill is built on the site of the Laurel Hill Estate. It opened around 1840 and is recognized as one of the most beautiful, and inviting, cemetaries in the country. Members of every old and noteworthy Philadelphia family are buried here as well as forty Civil War generals and other notables. And though Paris' Cimetiere du Pere Lachaise may have Balzac and Jim Morrison, Philadelphia's Laurel Hill has Adrienne Balboa. Reason to go while you're still alive? There is no better spot, not even Rittenhouse Square to lunch on a beautiful sunny day than here. And it isn't being disrespectful, it is encouraged. The old and some magnificent gravestones, markers and family mausoleums make fascinating sight seeing and not at all macabre. Forget that you think that this recommendation may have been written by Crispin Glover or other slightly off center character, its a good tip.

text: An amazing concept that delivers! I had wanted to try Luke for awhile now, but we couldn't get down to NO until this month.. Luke made it worth the wait.. My wife and I love France and the food, while Luke is a mix of classic French and German flair the French side is definitely the shining star here.. The decor is a bit simplistic, but in a good way. Light colored hardwoods and shared bench seating are both warm, comfortable and inviting. The menu is is a bit German, a good amount of French and a splash of Creole added. We started out with the gumbo which was perfectly balanced and seasoned well. I'm not a seafood lover and I have to say this was the best gumbo I have ever tasted, my wife agreed. Oh before I forget.. The French bread and butter were done so well it would have made Lionel Poilane smile.. For mains my wife had the crab ravioli and I had the ribeye, both were excellent. The pasta looked and tasted handmade and the sauce was creamy yet delicate, while the crab was fresh and large. The ribeye I had was great, I want to address the comment below about the ribeye being mostly fat.. Ribeyes are just that, a well marbled cut of meat which lends itself well to being slow roasted (Prime rib, Standing rib roast) when grilled the fat will be more prominent especially at lower temps.. Maybe he got a bad cut, but knowing your proteins is half the battle.. Back to the steak, I enjoyed my ribeye and the presentation on a wooden cutting board is a nice touch, however I did not care for the béarnaise sauce.. The fries were a bit salty for me, but I'm a hypersensitive to course salts so some might like them.. After brushing the salt off the taste was spot on and tasted like they were fried in a good oil not just plain ole veg. For dessert we split the bread pudding and were pleasantly surprised at the souffle style presentation.. The taste was good, however the ice cream could use some work and I would try another dessert next time.. Even with the ice cream, it's still a very, very good dessert, I'm just more of a chocolate lover.. Drinks at Luke are AMAZING! It's not the typical NO drinks, these are high end fine cocktails.. The French 75 is well worth the price of admission and the brandied cherries that are put in random drinks are out of this world good.. Also, any time someone goes to the trouble to put a super high end Italian steam pump espresso machine in his restaurant I'm impressed.. The latte my wife had was better than I can make at home using peaberry Jamaican blue mountain.. For the value, concept and variety this is one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans.. Five Stars

When I was in high school I was estatic to find out that I didn't need to drive all the way down to warminster anymore to get to this place. The rolls are usually pretty good, and they fill it decently enough with steak. There really isn't much to say about this place, but what I do really makes the stars disappear. I will get to that one option later on. I've had no problems with warminster, but here there seems to be major issues. The cheese steaks are decent. The buns are usually not toasted near enough and are not really Amoroso rolls, which makes Philly famous for its steaks. They fill the hoagie with a decent amount of steak so I have absolutely no complaints there, and if you get a special (the Stuffalo is my Fav and is awesome) steak it is usually pretty good. The one thing I noticed the other day, NONE of the staff EVER put on ANY gloves while handling food. I find this repulsive and almost wanted to say something because that is completely unacceptable. I honestly did not see a single staff member wear gloves, from the person grabbing my hoagie roll, to the other cooking the steaks and fries. NOBODY put on golves. I honestly would have rated this place a 3 or 4, but I am astounded at how none of the staff wear protective gloves to not only protect themselves, but the food they carry around. The place is also run by teenagers, I don't think I've ever seen a single person older then 19 here. Where are the managers? I also went on their website to file a complaint, and there's really no option to do so. And the phone number sends me to the doylestown "corporate office" which is probably just the joint itself. I honestly don't think I'm going to come here again, I've been here many times before and I do believe in multiple visits I don't see people wearing gloves...I'd love for a state health inspector to visit and audit this place because they would do HORRIBLY.

text: New Orleans Birthday Trip = Fauxdoo 2 in the French Quarter More liquor and random wanderings led us to Marie Laveau's, and, throwing caution to the wind, I hoped that maybe I'd find something, anything, better. Selection: A lot like Rev. Zombie's shop, meaning a lot of mistaken tourists will grab it all up as authentic. Yet again, there are some pieces here and there that do impress, especially their tribal statues, but what I found here was invaluable. It wasn't a trinket or a talisman, no potions or voodoo dolls. No, I found a goth gay. Now, normally, this would not be a sight to behold, his black makeup standard and bleached hair nonextreme, even his choice in feminine punk rock and gothic clothing were pretty normal, but he had information. My little gay goth drew me a map and all but jumped for joy when I asked if he knew a good apothecary we could go to. "Thank god," he said, "you're the first person in months to ask." So, there you go, a store worker even admitted that the House of Voodoo was fauxdoo. But still, that said, the selection at Marie Laveau's is more specific than Rev Zombie's. They, on average seem to have about a 22-78 ratio or real to fake, but they also have different things than RZ. If you're looking for souvenirs, then go to RZ or ML, they're about the same. If you're on the hunt for some real supplies, then try Island of Salvation, because that's what I found to be worth it. Venue: It's on Bourbon and that's all you need to know. You'll find it, keep wandering, look for a big bright voodoo sign. And then look real hard inside, you might find something worth buying.

text: If I could give a negative rating, I would. Worst customer service EVER. At a time, I imagine they could have up to 8 different exhibits. The architect, Randall Stout, has given this place more functionality than his ex-boss's (Frank Gehry) works of similar grace. The outside has a very Gehreisc resemblance to it looking almost like a younger brother of the Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles. The gift shop is cute! They have books on art, Edmonton, artists etc. along with the coffee mugs, jigsaw puzzles and the likes. Given that they have a sort-of childrens' section on the main floor, I think this place would be a good place for families. The guides and other people who work here are quite knowledgeable and clearly enthusiastic about their job. The only downside, as I see it, is that their exhibits don't change as often as they could. If it were an enormously large gallery, that would be a good thing. But given that the exhibit sizes are relatively small, I wish they'd have at least one new exhibit every 2 months.

text: 5 stars for the food, the environment, and the thoughtful service. It's a quaint country farmhouse converted to a wonderful, romantic restaurant, with tables spread throughout its many rooms, most of which have only a few tables providing an intimate, classic dining experience. The food is uniformly fantastic, from the classic Caesar salad prepared tableside, to the big, rich Maryland crab cakes wholly comprised of fresh crab meat and plated across a pair of spicy and pesto sauces. Lobster crepes (stuffed with equally massive amounts of lobster), truly rich lobster bisque, moist tender rack of lamb, and obscenely intense veal tenderloin with exotic mushroom sauce (a special) were equally brilliant examples. My only observation and minor nit about the food was that the meat was not precisely cooked - all the smaller medium-rare items were solidly medium, while the larger filet mignon, ordered medium, came out medium-rare. But all were delectable, and very tender. Desserts were equally brilliant, from the Belgian dark chocolate mousse to the Austrian cheese strudel. The wine list is reasonably large and well selected, especially considering the location, though the markup is enormous. Unfortunately, due to the exorbitant licensing fees charged by Pennsylvania, this is more or less unavoidable, and with a careful search (and sufficient knowledge) reasonable value items can be found. Service was friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable (though the average wine knowledge of the servers isn't large). If you're looking for a fantastic meal in an out-of-the-way, rusticly romantic environment, look no further. They also have a B&B with quite reasonably priced rooms on site.

text: I would have to say I have never been impressed with this hospital. I have had several relatives come in and out of here since it's the closest hospital in the area. Some for births and once my grandfather for ICU and later regular recovery from his illness once he came out of ICU. I have also had stitches here in the ER. I don't recall the trip to the ER's level of cleanliness but the wait was looooong. I had a head wound and was bleeding pretty well. The nurse and doctor I had on that visit were more than competent though. The nurse brought me a blanket because I was going into shock and stayed with myself and my mother (I was in high school at the time) until the doctor came. The doctor was pretty decent at stitching me up. I had a fairly small scar considering the extent of my injury. He was a little on the impatient side waiting for my anesthetic to set in though. I could still feel it a bit when he sewed me up (ouch). On the flip side: every time I have visited a relative here I have been more and more freaked out. 2 visits have been in the past 1-2 years. The more recent visit was for a relative who had a baby in May 2009. The wait to get into maternity ward is LONG. There's only one elevator in and out of the maternity wing and you have to stop at security and they take your license from you and give you a badge, want to know who you're going to see, etc. I can understand that but the guards are not very quick about it so a queue forms rather quickly. I went up 2-3 times over the course of 2-3 days and had to wait longer and longer each time. The other visit as I said was in ICU, Cardiac ICU in particular. You have to come to a waiting room and call the nurses desk to get in. This area is not nearly as "crazy" on security as Maternity. I went to visit my grandfather every day for a total of about 10 days and except for the first time no one even stopped me to ask where I was going when I was on my way to the waiting room. The ICU nurses were not to my expectation. Several times a medication would run out and begin beeping alerts and the nurse would not come. I have decent knowledge of medical equipment so I understand that the difference between "warning" type beeps when the meds are getting low and "ran out" beeping. I typically had to go GET a nurse to come refill a medication or fix whatever equipment was having a problem. When he was moved from ICU to regular admission rooms, no one had ANY idea where he was. Front desk originally directed me to ICU still and then the nurse on the waiting room phone advised me he was not there. I then had to go back to another service desk to ask where he was. Later he was moved from one regular room to another and during that move I had to stop and ask two nurses before someone would look it up and tell me where he was. Nothing scarier than walking into a room where your sick grandpa was last night when you left him and finding an empty bed! In his case in regular rooms, the nurses were TERRIBLE. It was obvious whoever did his IV lines was completely incompetent, he had HUGE bruises all over his arms and kept complaining that they would stick him over and over. As I said, he stayed in three rooms over his stay, one ICU, and two regular. All three of them were FILTHY. The food they brought him was pathetic. Also he said that nearly every time he asked to talk to his doctor about possible release (when he was back in a regular room and doing well) that he was flat out refused to even be allowed to discuss it. His insurance was good so they were interested in keeping him there as long as possible to get more money. They conveniently had a new reason he needed to stay every day. The whole hospital is horribly dirty really. The nurses are hit & miss. Some are sweet and caring and some obviously wish they had another job and don't mind making it obvious. Additions have been made randomly over time so the layout is a huge maze. No one is interested in helping you find the room you're looking for. If I am still living here when I have a child I will definitely be insisting on going to another hospital such as Tampa General or St. Josephs. I'd rather go to any hospital but here!

I think I saw some free street parking. Busyness - This is a pretty busy location. It's fairly close to downtown and just across from Grant MacEwan University. I would imagine that it gets even busier once school's back in. Noisiness - There's a nice high ceiling that seems to absorb the noise reasonably well. The music isn't too loud either. Ambience - I've been coming to this Starbucks for a couple of years and I've always liked it. Power - It is available, but the window seats and tables in the centre have an issue. I'd bring an extension cord if you want to use some of the tables in the centre. Free wifi - Available and works well. Being one of those people who keeps a number of tabs open, you might want to login with a browser which you don't use often, otherwise each page becomes a login page, oddly enough. (In Firefox Windows 7 at least.) Staff - Always friendly and helpful. I've rarely had a complaint about a Starbucks employee. Seating - There are 28 seats in this Starbucks, with four armchairs and two good sized tables for laying out a bit of work. I like the square tables they have here. They're at a nice height and are quite roomy, compared to the dinky round cafe tables I normally see at Starbucks. There are four or five tables outside on the spacious patio. It's also bordered by some hedges to give it a bit of privacy. I don't know if they ever use the patio heaters. Security - When I first started coming to this location, there was a homeless camp in the empty lot nearby. It's gone now, but the Starbucks is close to downtown. Not too bad of an area but 107 Ave is close by. Take the usual precautions.

text: I'm only rating the Oysters here. Sat at the bar, ordered a dozen of the East Coast. When I asked them where they were sourced to it took 10 minutes to get New York/New Jersey as an answer. That isn't an answer, by the way. It's not even a region. It's a number of regions lumped together. When pressed, it took 5 more minutes to get the bullshit answer; Bluepoint. Bluepoint is any oyster from any subspecies or locale in, you guessed it, New York or New Jersey. I guess it implies Long Island to the less educated, but I lived in Oyster Bay, Long Island (the biggest oyster fishery on the Island) for years and everyone whose eaten the real thing knows why real Long Island oysters are always marketed as such. They're the high end of the Bluepoint class and the reason it got its name. Naming and unknown sourcing aside, the shuck was just dirty enough to be unpleasant but not quite bad enough to send them back. The mignonette was bland. The actual oysters were flat and and tasteless. If they were Bluepoint at all, they were from southern waters. Probably a fishery somewhere in south Jersey. Do not eat oysters here.

text: I was in town for a research trip, so I needed to be close to the natural history museum. I booked the Agave Inn after seeing pictures of it on the internet. I abhor all things chain, and Agave Inn looked like it combined the eclectic decor with the value of marketed chain. It exceeded all expectations. It was cool and funky, with great style and youthful energy without going overboard. The beds... oh man. I could sleep all day in that bed. My room had a kitchen, and while it wasn't stocked by Williams and Sonoma, I didn't lack for anything. I felt like I had my own studio apartment. The room even had an ipod dock... and great views of the mountains (from my suite). The best part about the hotel is the staff. I can't even begin to tell you how friendly the lady is who works there. Sweetest smile I have ever gotten from that side of the counter. She really wanted to make sure that I had everything that I needed. She made sure the heat was right in my room by coming up and showing me. She got me real wine glasses so I didn't have to use platic cups. I loved her! In a nut shell, this hotel was fantastic. It was close enough to everything without making me feel like a tourist, and it was affordable enough that I got to spend my money on more important things (like wine). It wasn't overrun with college kids or pretentious rich old people. I would recommend this to people who want somewhere to stay that is special and unique, and that recognize that quality is best spent on rad employees and beds made from the clouds of heaven, rather than big lobbies or neon signs.

text: You know those mornings when the sun hits your pillow at the perfect angle and the sky is that special shade of clear, pale blue? When you're struck with the sudden urge to venture out into the city and soak it all in? A few weeks ago I woke up to one of those days, and although I'd been recovering from a cold, something deep within was crying out for dim sum, and I was sure I'd be able to muster up the energy for at least a few miles of sun-soaked strolling. There's also something hard-wired into my brain that prevents me from recalling the events of past ventures into China Town. Basically, it's never easy, and it for some reason never winds up actually involving walking. There's always some sort of time constraint/foot injury/purportedly brilliant lunch-with-grocery shopping combo that results in driving rather than walking. This time, my boyfriend busted his knee on our way out the door. Oops. Walking no longer an option. And driving means parking. Combine my already empty belly, plus all of the time spent driving around looking for a street space because it costs a whopping $5/HALF HOUR to park in a lot in those parts, plus my boyfriend's fear of secret chicken/pork in the seemingly seafood/veg dim sum options, and before you know it it's 2:00, you have a whopping headache, you can't decide on a restaurant, and the day suddenly seems dull and regular, instead of glimmering and full of promise. This is how we wound up at Kingdom of Vegetarians, and we settled on the dim sum all-you-can-eat sampler, for I believe $12. I'm not usually too picky when it comes to vegetarian chinese, but i gotta be honest-- if pre-made packets of doughy, unidentifiable veggie mush aren't your thing, then this isn't the meal for you. The chinese pizza was crispy with just enough scallions, and I should have gobbled it up when it was hot rather than holding out for the surprises to come. The tea was weak, with leaves floating in it, the veg. wonton soup that everybody raves about was undercooked, so the wontons remained hard little balls of dough stuffed with still-crunchy cabbage and other diced vegetables. There wasn't any dessert. All in all, I was underwhelmed. There are far better vegetarian chinese places in the city.

text: Cheers for strip mall Italian! Forget the ambience of the sit-down dining experience and stick with take-out. Fortunately, the pizza, if ordered fresh rather than by the slice, is top notch. Crispy crust, cheesy, fresh toppings. The house is a mid-century vintage prairie-style home. It has a triangular plan; triangles are definitely the concept here as they appear in the roof and patios too. Some of the windows are original stained glass, others look like they were used to shoot arrows out at invaders. (There were no invading hordes that day, just two perspiring design tourists with digital cameras). It is very well restored and preserved. If you are a big Wright fan, I recommend coming here. No, it's not as impressive as Falling Water or Taliesin, but it is a very thoughful and awe-inspiring design nonetheless.

text: The Castle has been, and continues to be, the one place that never really disappoints when I go out. Granted, that's mostly on Thursday or Monday nights, and not on their bread-and-butter goth nights, but still. If you've never been, the best way to describe it would be a two-story palace of sensory overload, complete with high-tech lighting, gothic decor, lightening-fast bartenders, huge sound systems, and plush couches, if your feet get tired.. To de-romanticize it for a moment: picture everything SOAKED in cigarette smoke, and then get the hell over it. I hate to say it, but you will not get noticed for what you're wearing unless you're just wearing fishnet and your hair is on fire (and maybe not then). The upside to this: everyone at the Castle is laissez-faire, so you can basically go out with friends and be totally yourself. It can get over-crowded, but I've never had a bad night because of the people there. Let me echo VJ Mike: this is NOT a "gay bar". Sunday nights are a gay-themed party (which is starting to play some real cutting edge stuff) and queer people show up here and there on each night, but if you don't mess with anyone, they're not going to mess with you. Labels really don't have a place at The Castle. In fact, the last time I was out, I found myself meeting an entire gang who usually run a straight-as-they-come country western bar. If you're that uptight that you think the Castle is a gay club, you might as well spend your nights watching "The Cosby Show" on TBS. Monday night is 80s/Progressive, which f**king rocks and has the most fulfilling dancefloor experience compared to busier nights. Thursday is Video/Electro/Pop, with some hip-hop and Lonely Island thrown in. I don't leave a Thursday without totally sweating through my clothes from dancing...it's a completely euphoric experience. Friday and Saturday are goth/fetish staples in Tampa. I don't have a leather harness and platform boots ready, so I tend not to show up for the mostly-industrial-dark-dance nights, although my friends just show up in jeans and t-shirts, so there you go. The place is cash only, which can suck, but they have an ATM (and with the sheer volume of people in and out, it's better that they don't mix your card up with someone else's). Every night tends to have some kind of drink special, but nothing is cheaper than $3. So, if you want a night out at a place where you can mix it up, move around, and possibly catch the inspiration to dance all night, hit the Castle.

Running out of that place with Lunchables stuffed in your pants is a rite of passage for Drexel Students who aren't on co-op. This Seven-11 was a proverbial showcase for all things Drexel; a perfect cross section of college life married with the charm of West Philly and urban culture. Its here that we met Smokey the Bum, the Boxer Bum, Cj the bum, Delonte West (of NBA Fame) and the Angry White Bum (of Angry White fame). On a side note, its funny and terrible that the Angry White Bum's (AWB) only distinguishing characteristics were the fact that he was angry, white and had a broken leg all 5 years I was in school - but that was enough distinction for him to stand out on campus from the other bums. Moving on... Even 5 years later, the staff is still anchored by Pele, Teltor and Subtor. These poor guys had the best sense of humor and always hooked us up with free taquitos. Pele did actually kick my friend one time when he wouldn't leave though. Unfortunately their hospitality ended the time we accidentally pulled all the credit card machines out of the counter, by accident. To this day they will still call the police on site of me or Bok Choi. Gosh, where's the sense of humor guys? Other facts you should know about this 7-11 1. It has 78 "blind spots". Rad. 2. If you dive into the ice cream cooler, it does not take you back in time, it just smashes all the ice cream. 3. If you go in the stock room and run around they don't appreciate it, no matter how "cool with them" you may be. 4. It's ony 3.5 blocks from the New Angle Lounge. 5. They only give you free taquitos to get rid of you. 6. They hate it when you offer to buy their uniform with Ultima Dollars. 7.They hate it when you walk behind the counter. 8. They hate it when you give them nicknames like Pele, Teltor and Subtor. 9.(#9 Deleted Due To Wife Spite) 10. Drexel Bike cops are always first on the scene and you can always outrun them - be sure to split before the guys with cars guns and real badges show up. Oh and avoid the dinty moore beef stew like the plague. They have had the same stock since '97.

text: I went to Chickie's and Pete's Cafe on a stopover to Philadelphia. I had two hours in between flights and wanted to take a cab over to Geno's but that was cutting it way too close. I figured hey this place must be pretty good since people have recommended it. I sat down and asked what they were famous for. They said that the crabfries were their trademark. I ordered those and a Philly Cheesesteak since I was in Philadelphia. The cheesesteak was good. It tasted authentic just similar to that of Pat's Famous Steaks off of Passyunk. The crabfries were tremendous. They had such great potatoe flavor. Also it came with a cheese dip that tasted great. My only gripe about this place is the service. I think the service here is pretty bad. At the end of my order I asked for a soda. My waitress said sure thing, and brought my check to me. I then asked for a soda again, thinking she forgot. I waited about 5-8 minutes and still no soda. I walked out with high hopes of a great experience shattered. The food is pretty decent here. I would probably avoid this place just for the service alone. The Philadelphia Airport is amazing. There are so many restaurants and shopping spots. The next time I'm in town, I'll be sure to visit another place as I probably will not go here again due to this bad service.

text: When you were a kid, did you ever invite your friends over, prepare a nice setting, and pretend you were rich and snobby while enjoying a can of Chef Boyardee? Well reminisce no more! All of this can be rekindled at Michelangelo's Ristorante Italiano. One evening I was invited to a small dinner party of 6 at one of Tucson's premier Italian dinning establishments. My sobering 20-30 minute drive could not prepare me for the ambiance and the food of this place. First of all, ladies and gentlemen, if you are single and in your 30's this is not the place to go if you wish to bump into that man or woman of similar background... unless you like the type of man or woman who already has one foot in the grave and the other one pushing a walker after leaving their BMW or Mercedes behind in the parking lot. That night, the party I was with were enjoying numerous professor sightings from the local university which made the discussion turn to current and past educational experiences. Michelangelo does boast a beautiful and relaxing ambiance and is an excellent place for a romantic and intimate 2nd date. Its moderate priced meals began first with either a soup or salad and bread. I believe I had the ever so common Minestrone which was prepared also with beans and from a nice can paste. Others enjoyed a modest sample of salad. Those who ordered the soup were more content than those who ordered the salad. Then the main dish arrived, mine was some kind of spinach ravioli concoction with cheese , sauce, and it all had a fancy poo-poo name. This fabulous dish was also made from fresh can tomato paste/sauce. I think the only thing that was truly fresh was the basil leaf of which they proudly adorned atop of my mozzarella coated ravioli. Those of us who ordered dessert that night truly enjoyed it. Overall, this restaurant is intended for those of a mature audience (someone who knows the difference between the salad fork and the dessert fork because they throw all the utensils at you). Screaming kids might disturb the ambiance and natives a little too much. There was much thought in the menu, but not the same in the preparation. Olive Garden and or Macaroni Grill would have been other excellent alternatives, but if you wanted an intimate and beautiful surrounding, money to throw away, and/or a date to impress, I would definitely give this place high consideration. Playa Alert: For those who have more than one love interest, this is an excellent restaurant to take the "other" for dinner especially if you belong to the 20-38 age group because the other kept person (and none of your friends) would never think of finding you here. Plus, you will make a strong false impression of possessing culture and intellect.
label: NEG

text: Billy Reid is not just an upscale shopping destination here in Nashville but a critically acclaimed designer that has been featured in many media publications, runways, and has a nice celeb following. Don't know if you care about those types of things....I happen to! I have recalled viewing stand out pieces in Esquire, Lucky, and Women's Wear Daily recently but hadn't had an opportunity to visit the Nashville shop yet. There are 6 locations total that include the flagship store in Florence, AL and upward to NYC. Diverse right? This location sells both the Men's + Women's collections in a richly posh space that includes a library littered with books, memorabilia, and sprinkled perfectly with merchandise. Although the space is not large, it possesses such a grand aesthetic. I was finally able to check Billy Reid out in the flesh last night because the store was hosting a benefit for the Belcourt Theatre. I became flat out smitten with the Women's Bowtie Blouses ($245) and Knit Ruffle Tops ($175). The Men's Raw Selvedge Levi's ($178) were classic in a very James Dean kind of way and made me whine for a pair to share with guy. Many of the weathered Men's denim shirts ($150) were also something that I could see my boyfriend wear but he would have flinched at the price tag. Men's jackets average around $600 and shoes average around $450. Billy Reid is not for those on a budget but for those who invest in clothing that they love and plan to keep around for years to come. The collection is not trendy but has an effortless style that is still very much on point. I live a Vegan lifestyle so all of the leather goods and coats made from Nutria fur certainly don't appeal to me. The leather boots and shoes seem to draw a large following however. Pricey but very polished. No. I'm not talking about me. Billy Reid...silly.
