text: It was an establishment of no small stature, the coffee shop that had for some time threatened to wrest the hands of the Bongo Java Roasting Company from about Nashville's underdeveloped little neck. This building was of course not the first of its kind. There was that one just off of West End, and then the one in 12 South, the one that had started it all by finally holding up its coffee condoms and its white paper cups in triumphant defiance of the norm. But this one, it was in EAST Nashville, just down the road from their humble apartment. Yes, this one belonged to them. They both needed coffee that night. After all, she had never seen Buffy the Vampire Slayer, and he was determined to get through the first season that day so that they could move on to the meatier stuff. The only thing they were missing for their Buffython was some coffee to help hold off the slumber. Unfortunately for the young couple, their coffee maker was for some reason brewing coffee that tasted as though it had been percolated in a garbage can. Have no fear though, for the Portland Brew is right down the road. So for a moment Buffy and her intrepid gang were left behind for the sweet lure of the bean. They arrived and opened the door they had opened so many times before, only this time something was dreadfully wrong. U2 was playing over the shop's sound system. And not even early U2, those albums wrought with political tension, that some part of you hates to admit are at least passable as early 80s post punk. No, this was the U2 that had unfortunately survived the 90s and emerged as a testament to one man's ego and one band's mediocrity. Standing behind the bar listening to Bono belt it out was a youth of the shaggy blond hair variety. The kind of kid who bought every Beatles and Hendrix shirt he could find at Target. He stood with his back turned, perhaps asleep, perhaps just so moved by Ireland's favored son (...) that he could not wrest himself from his home against the counter. The young couple exchanged silent glances with one another, trying to figure out what the deal was. Neither of them knew. He knocked on the counter top, but there was still no response. Maybe the young man was narcoleptic? Just when they thought they might scream, literally, as it seemed the only method with which to rouse this young man, another soul came around the corner, cast a glance at his cherubic friend, and then mercifully turned down the U2. He arrived at the register, fielded their orders, and then went to work. The man filled his coffee cup with some half and half and a dark roast which was utterly forgettable while the barista, apparently dressed for the nines in his fake motorcycle rider boots, black jeans, denim communist revolutionary hat, and yes, a Black Rebel Motorcycle Club t-shirt, prepared the lady's drink. I believe it was some sort of Black Rebel Motorcycle Club outfit, and neither the boy nor girl were certain if he had put it together himself or simply bought it prepackaged. So BRMC fan made her Americano, after again asking her what kind of flavoring she wanted in it, and finally the couple were off. Back in their home, sitting in front of the warm glow of the boy's laptop, huddled closely together after two large cups of coffee and watching Buffy and crew whomp some vampy ass, both of them silently wished that their was a chosen one out there to fight the forces of mediocre coffee.

text: A one and a half star experience for this location. A far cry from what we've experienced at other Crabby Bill's locations. We've been to one of the other Crabby Bill's locations a number of times and always had a great experience. The other diners we were with had been to this location before and had pleasant enough experiences. I don't know what happened tonight, but it wasn't good. We arrived at just before 8pm and got on the waiting list for a table of 5. Unfortunately, the restaurant only has two tables large enough to seat five without moving tables together, so we had to wait. And wait some more. After a while, we asked to make sure they hadn't forgotten about us. They reassured us that it would be just a few more minutes. Eventually, a couple of tables cleared and they could shuffle two tables next to each other. Without exaggerating, it actually took 3 people to do this. These aren't heavy tables, so I don't really know why it took 3 people, but ok. The first thing that struck us was that this place didn't feel like a Crabby Bill's. Normally, Crabby Bill's feels like a homey seafood restaurant. This location was built in what felt like a garage or storeroom. Looking up, you could see the ductwork. Everything felt very clinical, with some ocean themed decorations thrown on because it's a seafood restaurant. The waitress came by and let us know that they had some new margarita, which most of us ordered. It was a bit crowded and busy, but 15 minutes seemed like an awful long time to wait for our four margaritas. When they arrived, they tasted mostly of sour mix. Definitely not worth the $7 each. Upon looking at the menu, we were immediately surprised at how small it was. Maybe half the size of the St Pete location we normally visit. The others commented that it was smaller than the times they had been to this particular location before. We ordered a couple of appetizers: crabbyfeller oysters and some sort of shrimp (which I did not try). The crabbyfeller oysters were described on the menu as having a spinach dip, some cheese and then being baked. Our friends had ordered these at a different location before. When they came out, the first thing we noticed was that they were covered in bacon. Oysters - covered in bacon. Now, bacon may make most things better, but pescetarians don't eat bacon. The waitress noticed our horror and confusion on our faces and asked if something was wrong. "I guess I didn't realize there was bacon on these oysters. Are these the right ones?" "Yes, the crabbyfellers have bacon, it's the clevelanders that don't" "We wanted the ones with the spinach dip" "That's the crabbyfellers. They normally have bacon, but I can ask them to make them without it. Would you like that? It's no problem." And so, the bacon covered oysters went back to the kitchen. Meanwhile, I grabbed a menu. Lo and behold - none of the oyster options mentioned bacon -anywhere-. When the waitress returned, I pointed this fact out to her. "Oh, that's a typo. But we're trained that they have bacon on them. I'll tell the manager and the cooks that the menus don't mention it though." Eventually, the oysters came back without bacon. They were alright. The spinach dip flavor was nice, but the cheddar cheese was unnecessary. Apparently, other locations serve it as oysters, spinach dip and a bit of grated parmesan which sounds much more appetizing than what we got. The appetizer debacle aside, how were the entrees? Our friends found them acceptable, but not up to the quality level we've grown accustomed to from Crabby Bills. My wife ordered a rare grilled tuna steak which came out crusted in Old Bay spice and cooked medium. My clam strips were slightly undercooked and a little soft. By this point though, we knew we would be tempting fate sending anything else back to the kitchen. I grabbed some cocktail sauce from the squeeze bottle for my clams and immediately had to check to make sure it wasn't ketchup. It was super runny and watery. Tasting it, there was only the slightest hint of horseradish. We checked another bottle - and it was the same. When it came time to tip, I commented that "Food aside, the waitress was nice and really apologetic." My wife countered that when we were first seated, she overheard the waitress complaining about having to serve us to the manager. We only came to this location because it was the most convenient for a friend visiting town. Even he said he'd rather just drive the extra 20-30 minutes next time and avoid this location.

text: After a night spent bopping heads at a swank jazz club downtown (Sweet Lorraine's), and a handwritten list of places to try for brunch provided by the hostess, we settled on LPK as the place to try, mostly because of the name. We arrived at 10:45 to find that it didn't open til 11:00. Attempting to pass the time by hitting up one of the drive through daiquiri stands, we were relieved to discover that they were not open til noon. Way to have some class, New Orleans. 11:00 clicked in, the front door was unlocked, and we were the first into the empty restaurant. Payment was simple, prix-fixe settled before you approached the buffet. The initial buffet browse was promising, everything looked good except for the paltry chopped salad. I wasn't worried, because who goes to a creole brunch buffet looking for a nice fresh salad? I dished myself a sampler platter and tucked in. My smile grew with every bite. Crab and Corn chowder was a perfect balance of cream and salt, while creole shrimp had just enough kick to compliment the rice they were spooned over. The fried chicken was amazing - my friend bequeathed it the honor of 'best ever,' and lit a slow burn on the back of your tongue after the first few bites. White beans and sausage were perfectly cooked and richly flavored. My personal favorite was the carrot souffle, which I quickly realized was maybe an eighth carrot. The other 87% was flour, sugar, and eggs. It tasted like a fluffy sweet potato pie with a vegetal finish. Desserty, but not as desserty as the bread pudding with a vanilla brandy sauce. I ate til I couldn't move, and then had a last plateful. Go there.
label: POS

text: I was here last night primarily for some beer...food was a big maybe. I beat the rush by a bit so I was seated immediately, and my server was over promptly. I drank their Abbey Dubbel, which was rather good...not the best I've had by any measure but better than I was expecting. Nice head and smooth aftertaste. Bonus points there. My companion had their pumpkin ale, which while not as pumpkin-y as others I've had (Rock Bottom), was also not as "fruity", and had a bit more texture to it. We ended up getting the sweet potato fries and carrot soup, both of which were "good", but not "great". For the prices, they could/should have been a bit better...not sure I'm in a big rush to try for a full dinner at this point. But I was there for beer and they delivered...seemed to have a good amount of variety available, and I'm looking forward to trying out what else they have on offer. I suppose it is brewpub law that the food cannot overshadow the beer, and that it must be priced too high and given an air of luxury it simply doesn't deserve, so I won't get too upset about that part. I'm used to it. Iron Hill is a solid choice for that niche if you are in the North Wales area.

text: Two words, RIP-OFF. When i first walked into the place I thought that I'd died and gone to heaven. It really seemed like a paradise for true beer lovers. The first beer i ordered was a Celebrator Dopplebock , my girlfriend had the upland wheat. Her beer was on draft and was presented in the proper tall tapered wheat beer glass, our server dumped my beer ice cold into a standard shaker style pint glass and was extra careful to leave absolutely no head at all. Anyone who knows anything about good beer knows that this is wrong. My girlfriend ordered a basket of cheese sticks and we ate those while i waited for my beer to warm up to an enjoyable temperature. My next beer was the imperial gonzo porter from the flying dog brewery in colorado. This time i asked if i could pour the beer myself and our server was more than happy to let me do so, after i let it warm up. My girlfriend continued with her upland wheat. To top the evening off i had myself an old rasputin imperial russian stout, and our server was more than happy to bring me a snifter to pour this beer into. I let him know that this would be my last beer and that we were ready for the check. The grand total for one upland wheat, a celebrator, a gonzo porter, an old rasputin, and an order of cheese sticks came to just over $42.00!! We didnt spend that much for dinner plus two beers each at Brugge Brasserie. Point being, the owners of this place are exploiting peoples love of craft beer by gouging prices. $9.50 for an arrogant bastard ale? $7.00 for a schnieder weisse? If you want the real beer experience but dont want your wallet to be brutally beaten and raped into submission do yourself a favor and go to either party pack, or payless liquor and buy a six pack or two for the price of one beer at shallos and have yourself an honest to goodness drinking session at home among good friends.

I got the Usual- Roast Beef on Kaiser, with a wee bit of mayo, and what-the-hell throw on some Roasted Peppers and a slice o'cheddar. Mom got a Veggie Shortie and a diet Peach Snapple. Oh, she was in Heaven. (They don't have diet Peach Snapple at the cafeteria @ work.) Overall the place was clean. The staff seemed friendly, and were sporting their new tie-dye HOAGIE T-shirts (cute, can I HAVE one?) Cashiers were quick to get us rung up and outta there. Sandwich folks were singing along to the oldies while whipping up everyone's chow. Seems one guy called out for a "family emergency'. Poor guy missed all the fun. The sandwiches were fabulous, and not just b/c we were hungry enough to eat the paper they came in. They have moved the napkins right by the touch screens, so you can get 'em and go. Clever. The only 'icky' was that they had the door to the cleaning closet propped open, and were taking turns to come outside and squat on a milk carton to smoke. Watch the traffic around the gas pumps. Folks are in a hurry to get the hell in and out and don't take turns. On the whole, a sweet Wa experience.

text: I went to Osteria with high expectations. A friend with taste recommended it as a hot Philadelphia restaurant. I have to say my reaction was mixed. First impressions were strong: big, but cozy room, warm reception, friendly servers, and everything on the menu sounded great. I really liked the wine list: about a dozen Italian varietals by the glass, many good ones. I had a hard time choosing what I wanted for dinner, but ended up with a salad of raddichio, pear, and blue cheese and rabbit casalinga for the main course. As I watched the food coming to neighboring tables, I was really sorry that I wasn't dining with friends: it looked great! While the salad was fine--fresh, reasonable portion, well-dressed--the rabbit was a disappointment. Served on a bed of polenta, it was largely flavorless. I'm not quite sure how it became such a house favorite based on what I ate. I ordered a side of the celery root gratin, which was terrific. Plus the wait staff cleared my salad plate and dropped my entree in its place. Literally no pause between courses to catch my breath or take a sip of wine. What's with that? Liked the dessert list a lot, but I opted for an espresso and no dessert. Should have skipped the espresso--it was weak, almost without crema. Not what I'd expect from a to[-notch Italian restaurant. Having said this, I'm aware that this was one person's experience, on one night. I liked the menu and wine list a lot and I'd go back and give Osteria a second try. Hoping for better when I do.

This recent outing I ordered the sushi deluxe platter, which offered various sushi rolls along with sashimi. As usual the food was excellent. Mixx is a great place to sample from friend's plate to try new things (unless you get the unlimited sushi platter, in which case you aren't allowed to share). The staff here is beyond amenable, always courteous. They graciously added another table to accommodate dinner crashers such as myself. Mixx is a highlight of Chinatown, and an absolute must whenever you're in the area.

text: Let me start off by saying that I work and have worked in the medical field for 8 years as an office manager of a very busy and elite medical office. My husband and I moved so I was forced to switch dentists about a year ago and when I went to my first (and only) visit at Liberty Dental, I was put through the whole routine of the exam, x-rays and cleaning. The exam and cleaning were routine and the x-rays were as uncomfortable and took as long as one might expect. I met with Dr. Singh at the end of the visit. He proceeded to tell me that I should redo my fillings to "newer, white fillings" because they are more aesthetically pleasing. I did not think that I needed to go through the pain and spend the money on parts of my mouth that only I would be seeing. So, I declined the procedures. A couple of months later, my husband had to cancel an appointment because he was called for a job interview. He called on a Saturday at about 4:00pm (right after he received the date and time of the interview) to cancel his Monday appointment. He was called on Monday to say that he would be charged a $100 late cancel fee because it was the second time he canceled - the first being when his car broke down and he had to call AAA to get his car to a dealership to get a new battery. I advised him to question the $100 fee, which is the highest late cancel fee I've ever heard of. The office manager, Diane, spoke very rudely to him and said he didn't have a choice but to pay. My husband then spoke to Dr. Sing and the doctor said that he had no part in the policy and he then proceeded to give my husband a lecture on being more responsible. Well, just imagine saying to an interviewer of a prospective job that you can't do your interview that day because you have a dentist appointment. I don't know about everyone else, but if someone said that to me at work I would cross their name off the list. All in all, the office would not budge and is still requiring that we pay the $100 late cancel fee. Unbelievable that they are willing to lose two patients, hundreds of dollars of health insurance reimbursement plus numerous referrals for a late cancel fee. She indicated with her hands about a softball-sized portion, so we decided against paying $7 each for salads and ordered the Balsamic Onion to start, just to try something different. The Balsamic Onion was quite good and was more like a salad (slices of sauteed onion in a thick balsamic dressing), even pleasing my dinner companions who wouldn't normally touch such things as onions.... We ordered the Sausage Pizza and the Spinach Pizza. The pizzas weren't bad, not the best I've had by far, but for the price I was expecting more. The pies were small and I don't like when the crust starts competing with the cheese, sauce and toppings. If you're gonna give me a small pie, give me one that takes the good stuff all the way to the edge. The Spinach pie was preferred over the Sausage at my table; the long hot pesto on the Sausage pie was a little much at times and interfered with the sausage. We skipped on dessert, though the table behind us was gushing over their gelato. Bottom line, even though I'm a few blocks from Pizzeria Stella, I'm still going to make the trek to Mama Palma's in Filter's Square for my "gourmet" pizza, but if Starr kicks it up a notch here, I'll be back.

text: Let's face it folks, dining is about service, you go there to eat, but you also go there to have a good time. I planned to have my 18th birthday dinner at the California Pizza Kitchen. I had lots of friends say there were going to show up, and so I tried to reserve a big table, and for the most part the CPK was very responsive and nice about it. Until I actually showed up. Some people didn't come, or kept saying there were coming but didn't. And the management hassled me everyone couple of minutes asking if the whole party was going to arrive soon. I eventually figured out they wanted tables and told them to just take them, and some of the hassling stopped. I understand they need the tables for business, but if they really weren't supposed to sit people without their party, I would have been happy dividing my party to avoid the hassling. And on my birthday only annoys me more. But even the waiter was still ridiculously rude to my party. He claims they have a company policy that doesn't allow them to sing happy birthday or do anything for anyones birthday. Clearly this was a lie, because at the front, the hostess was telling me about a fudge cake I would get since it was my birthday, and then he had THE NERVE to come up to us and ask me if I wanted to BUY desert from them...for my birthday. Okay....NO. I don't know if he had ants in his pants or something, but he would stroll by every two to three minutes and ask how everything was doing, like he didn't have other customers to deal with, and even when he came he didn't pick up your drink for a refill, up to twenty minutes after it was empty. It was a horrible experience for me to spend, and even wasn't completely their fault, since I did have party cancellations, they didn't have to react the way they did, and I still ordered so much food that it's not like the waiter and restaurant didn't make a pile of money off my party and myself. If there's anything saving this place from one star it has to be that the food was still amazingly good, and that is about it. Restaurants can't just live off of good food though, they have to keep good clients and reputations to keep business going, and if I ever want to eat California Pizza Kitchen again in Brandon, I swear I will instead take it to go and just leave, screw the service there out of tips, and I will be sure to review them where ever I have an account to do so.

After some complaining we were seated outside at a small table with mis-matched chairs. The waiter was quite verbose, we received appetizers within about 20 minutes but it did take an hour and half to receive our entrees. The waiter apologized several times that the kitchen was backed up. We ordered a paella type dish, 2 scallop plates and a fluke. All were mediocre at best and each member of our party had expressed that individually. The scallops were not much better than I could have cooked them myself and the fries and grilled vegetable were luke warm and not exciting at all. My paella type dish was very bland and lacked complexity. I had acid burn on my tongue when I left the restaurant because of the amount of lemon I had to squeeze on it to give it some flavor. The fluke was incredibly sweet and lacked any acid or heat to mellow it out. Parties that were seated after us were told right away that there would be a long wait for their food. We all felt disappointed in the food and that we had paid $25 for parking on South Street to avoid missing our reservation. We were not at all eager to try dessert even though it was my birthday. text: We had high expectations given the first impression upon walking in (and by the Yelp reviews), but E&E disappointed on almost every note. We went early on a Tuesday and were seated right away. The interior is modern and hip, with cozy tall (overhead) round booths. The service was friendly and not overbearing. We started with the ahi sashimi appetizer and iceberg wedge. The sashimi was well seared, but was drizzled with a wasabi based sauce and another mild chili red sauce. It looked great, but I could have done without the sauces. Ahi tuna is a delicate taste, and was washed out by the oversaucing. The seaweed salad and ginger on the side were a nice and proper touch. The iceberg wedge was simply an iceberg lettuce head, quartered, and served with a blue cheese dressing and some grape tomatoes. The dressing was notable, but otherwise the dish was not. Our dinner specials came with caesar salads (the house salad-- which I found odd). I ordered mine with dressing on the side, and I'm glad I did. What came out was some chopped lettuce (romaine), with a smattering of grated parmesan, and (inexplicably) some multicolored tortilla strips. The dressing in the side cup was unappetizing, looking like oil mixed with mayonnaise. We should have taken the salads as a bellwether. When the entrees arrived, they were plated well, but many little things added up to a hot (overcooked) mess. The lobster tail was chewy and overcooked. There was some kind of breaded chunk atop the lobster tail reminiscent of a "Rockefeller" treatment, which tasted fine, but I didn't get why it was there. The sweet potato mash had apples mixed in, and was cloying (sweet potatoes don't need another fruit to make them taste good; take a cue from the name, chef!) The crab cake was the best part, with lump crabmeat, but it had the same drizzle as the sashimi app. Most of the spices and flavors they used were just "off." Too much going on on the plate. The veg on both entrees was a mix of steamed broccoli, julienned carrots in some kind of sweet sauce, and edamame (flavorless and out of place on the plate). The flounder piccata, while simpler, was also overcooked. It had the piccata sauce, but also some kind of smoky barbeque sauce drizzled alongside it. The corn mashed potatoes had a similar "off" spice/seasoning. The burger was cooked medium well (correctly) and the fries reminded me of Checkers fries, with an extra crispiness to them (perhaps finished in a convection oven). The shift manager walked by once during the early part of the meal to ask how everything was. He barely broke his stride to actually wait for our reply, so at that time we did not have a composed answer. A few minutes later, we did let the server know about the overcooked dishes, and he offered one free dessert. We opted for the bread pudding, which was on the special menu. It was fine, but served in an overly sweet caramel sauce. To top it off, there is a compulsory 15% gratuity "for your convenience" (that was actually printed on the check). They've probably been stiffed by Canadian snowbirds who don't customarily tip, but restaurants that don't respect their patrons enough to tip properly leave a bad taste in my mouth. Couple that with the *ACTUAL* bad taste in my mouth from the many mistakes that were made on the plate, and the high prices, and you understand the two star rating.

Bottom line is they were charging me for each technician visit. I said that I understood that technician visits were included in my service. She just looked at me and said, "yes". text: Pari, how I lurrrrrve thee. Given the hit-or-miss quality of the food around the Penn campus, this is one place in which I can have confidence that I will get a quality, fresh food dish. And it is consistently good. The modular nature of this food and the willingness of the staff to accommodate your needs is what wins us over. Their menu selections are suggestions--if you want to modify something, say you want an egg white omelette instead of the whole egg on your crepe, they will make it for you. You can choose as many, or as few, of the fillings as you want, so you can get a truly customized meal. Just tell them light cheese, extra cheese, light sauce, extra sauce, whatever suits you--and they listen. Sometimes I get just an egg and cheese crepe and they don't charge full price for those, which is nice. And if you just want an omelette and no dough, they will fix that too. You can also choose from three different crepe batters--herb, honey wheat, and hardstone white. I am a fan of honey wheat myself. This place is great for a weekend brunch when the waits are short and Houston Hall is quiet. Given the lack of good breakfast places around the campus, give this a try if you long for something like pancakes. The crepe batter isn't sweet, but combined with fresh fruits and some sweet sauce like caramel or honey or chocolate makes it come darn close. Again, the honey wheat is my favorite batter, and paired with the sweet fruit and sauce is so incredibly good. I will caution vegetarians (as I am one myself) to kindly ask the staff if they will wipe the grill and the little bowls in which they hold the fillings before putting them on the crepe as sometimes meat pieces will get mixed in. That's really my only complaint, and that's pretty minor overall and easily solvable. Fruit for the sweet crepes is cut up directly over your freshly cooked crepe batter. I only wish they also had tofu as a filling option too! Something like a tofu teriyaki crepe with veggies might be a nice addition to the menu. Or a veggie burrito crepe with tofu.

text: I rarely go to Lazy Acres these days, and although the quality of their stuff is good, there are closer options for good produce than making the trip over to the Mesa. There are, however, a couple key items that Lazy Acres stocks that I can find nowhere else, or haven't yet located elsewhere. The assorted cuts of grassfed beef, as noted in my first review, and also Electro-Mix, a sugar free sports drink mix put out by the same folks that make Emergen-C, and a terribly yummy Dutch cheese called Beemster. A friend bought me a fat wedge of classic Beemster after she tried some at a Christmas party. It's aged a minimum of 18 months, tastes dense, tangy and nutty, pairing well with wine, or port. Delicious to just eat as little slices, melting on your tongue. So, I received that cheese last December, and I cut away at it all year. Eight months later, I still have a good knob and it's remained in decent condition, just less moisture content now. I grated it into a fine soft pile with a microplane and it can now be mixed in dressings, sprinkled on grilled vegetables, and used in place of parmigiano reggiano with the similar sharp tang, but different flavor. If this kind of cheese intrigues you, scamper on down to Lazy Acres. Note: I have shied away from the ready-meal deli section. It looks good, but two friends of mine who've bought stuff from that section twice, each got dysentery twice afterwards and had never suffered from that before, and have never gotten it since. My stomach is made of pretty stern stuff, but I'm no fool to play with those odds.

text: We have been looking forward to eating here ever since we moved to Nashville. After several failed attempts and canceled reservations, we finally went to celebrate a birthday. To cut to the chase, the food was inconsistent. Not all of it was bad, but, at a place like The Standard, you would expect so much more of it to be good. And, unfortunately, the same could be said for the entire dining experience. The only memorable thing about the food was our appetizers. I had the grit cake with crayfish, which was really excellent. It was an imaginative interpretation of Southern cuisine. The grit cake was crispy with a wonderful flourish of corn and a nice sizable portion of crayfish. My dinner companion had the mushrooms in a pastry puff, which was also very good, even for me who does not normally like mushrooms. Now, if we would've stopped here, we would be raving about this restaurant. Unfortunately, we proceeded like normal folk to the entrees. I got their house specialty, Bacon-Bacon, which is supposed to be a bacon wrapped pork loin. However, I wouldn't call it a pork loin or a medallion or anything I would've expected to see bacon wrapped around. It was more like a thin pork chop (reminded me of what I would buy at Aldi or Kroger in bulk meat) with barbecue sauce(!!) on it and plated on top of an unappetizing mix of bacon bits, beans and corn. I guess that's the succotash. And my entrée was better than my dinner companion's, who had the seared duck with a confusing mix of over-seasoned asparagus tips, undercooked black beans and a corn fritter. The duck was also stringy and fatty. Both of us ordered a glass of wine and we both ended up with our second choice since there were no open bottles of our first choices. Okay. The service was fine and polite, and we never felt rushed. However, there seemed to be only 1 or 2 waiters and a bus boy the entire night, resulting in a lot of rushing from table to table and brief queries about our food and if we needed anything. The outside of the restaurant looks very charming with its small courtyard in front. However, the ambiance inside of the restaurant and dining area lacks warmth and intimacy. And I realize I'm being very nit-picky here but I was bothered by their "artwork." Here you have a historic, mid-19th century townhouse and they have a bunch of black-and-white photographs of women's bodies from the neck down. Not nude or erotic in any manner, but just ... really cheesy. It reminded me of a woman's Casual Corner catalog. How about some framed photos of historic sites in Nashville, photos of the restaurant being renovated, or even photos of past and prominent Nashvilleans? The Standard offers itself up to be a fine dining experience, but it just doesn't succeed in enough categories. Call me fastidious or overly critical, but, if you're going to get all gussied up and pony up $100 for two for dinner, wouldn't you expect more?
label: NEG

text: Okay. I'm going to try and keep this simple: For a hotel of this size, nameplate and cost per room this hotel is a complete failure. Approaching the hotel, it looks pretty modern and nice. It's next to what seems like a high-end mall for the WASPy suburbanite inside of you but if you don't use the valet, you have to drive around to the back B-level entrance where you get all the charm of a hospital emergency room. The lobby is pretty nice and the staff were pleasant and helpful. Like other reviewers they dropped the "remodel is coming" stuff. I got my key and headed to my room where I noticed that there were several displays with fabric and carpet swatches with renderings of said remodel. Whootpie-do! What good does that do me? Am I supposed to use my imagination and make believe when I get to my room? Which leads me to the next point... It's very easy to use your imagination when you get into your room because there is no light switch anywhere near the door so you're in complete darkness if you check in after sundown! Try and picture that earlier rendering because you're going to have to Stevie Wonder your way around the room until you stumble into the bathroom, the only place where I found a switch Bed was clean but old. Springs were hard and creaky. Hot water took about 5 minutes or more to get going (6:30 AM on a Sunday, maybe I was the first to shower). TV had all the classic hotel room channels plus the obligatory staticy channels. I've never understood why every hotel in the US has at least a couple channels with weak signal but I digress. No free wifi (hard wired internet was also at a cost). No free coffee that I was aware of. I peaked at their breakfast menu and when I saw the 8 dollar oatmeal I got my trusty (except for calls) iPhone out and yelped to the stellar Cafe Patachou. So in short, this is an awesome Motel and a lousy Hotel. Shop around.

text: A few years ago Mr Q and I took a trip to NOLA. A friend of mine had recommended Bloody Mary's nighttime cemetery tour as being really good & interesting, so we signed up online, I paid by Paypal, and provided contact info in case anything changed. Fast forward to the actual night of the tour..it was a bit out of the way and closer to the skeevy part of town than we would have liked, so we shelled out $$ to take a cab. Cab drops up off in front of the appointed meeting place...but no one is there to meet us. We wait, along with one other group of 3. After waiting for around 20 minutes, someone discovered a small handwritten sign taped low down on a chain link fence that said something to the effect of "Bloody Mary is having legal issues and won't be able to give the tour. If you would like a refund, please call the number below" I'M SORRY? No call to let us know, no refund in advance, we were dropped off in the middle of the ghetto at night time with only the dead surrounding us. Anyway we hopped the fence to one of the cemeteries and took pictures in the dark but it wasn't *quite* the same. Oh and did I mention that this was not exactly a popular cab pick-up spot? We waited a LONG time for the trolley to pick us up. Zero stars for not letting us know before we wandered out there like a couple of assholes in the dark.

I have been here a few times and feel that the experiences have been identical. Long wait ( in a small area), service that is a snail's pace, and food that is underwhelming. My pizzas, even the marherita (which is probably the simplest one on the menu), usually come out crusty (in a bad way), congealed, and cold. Not really what I want for the amount of money you have to spend. On a positive note....this place is pretty clean (even for my crazy OCD standards). I enjoy the way the main dining area is set up with high ceilings, bright colors, and funky accents. Unfortunately, it is just not enough to make me enjoy CPK.

Lamb arrived warm, but not warm enough - chantrelles risotto was flavorful, but nothing special. My wife was told that the plate that held her chicken dish was hot (meaning it was under some sort of heat source - unacceptable at these prices). She noted that the dish lacked flavor. Our cocktails were really good and we enjoyed our shared dessert. Ambience was nice, but it was a little too dark - hard to read the menu and see the food when it was served. The service was pretty attentive. Had a nice bottle of wine that seemed reasonably priced. Have lived in the area for 8 years and have been wanting to visit here for some time - it just seemed to let us down - for what we paid we could have had TWO excellent dinners at a local restaurant in Malvern, West Chester or Phoenixville. text: Dinner the weekend of 5/01. Saturday night. Late seating, say 7:30ish. Our party of six did not wait long since we had dropped our name about 30 minutes prior and walked over to Jolly Piano for a quick drink. Our waitress was extremely pleasant and helpful ( the only thing which bumps my star rating from one to two), however that's where the goodness stops. I have never been a fan of "auctioning" food and that's what a swarm of attendants did. And they forgot an entree long enough that it was uncomfortable not eating while waiting until all were served. I ordered the Tamales. Granted I have never had tamales before, so maybe they are supposed to be soggy. And taste like flour. Have no flavor ( besides flour). So I pushed those aside and ordered what I thought would be a safe bet to munch on: Queso Chorizo Fundido. Wrong again. The cheese was so thick I had to cut it to manage it, and even then it was quite difficult. It was so heavy and oily that I pushed that aside as well. During my little debacle, while I was still eating, one of the attendants started clearing the table. Actually tried to grab a plate out from under me as I was using it. Really? Really? I mentioned that this was a Saturday night for this reason: One could infer that this was their way of flipping the table quickly to accommodate other parties. Not the case. There were about four empty tables in our section. So to me, no reason whatsoever for the running of the bulls. I was left as the obvious last eater and was asked several times, are you still using that? Are you finished with that? The third time I was asked, I surrendered. This time it was our waitress asking, so I guess they sent the big guns. She noticed my scarcely eaten plates and I did comment on how I did not like either dish. She could not have been nicer or more accommodating and brought me out ice cream on the house. The manager came over and attempted to make nice as well, but by this time I just wanted to get out of there. Oh, and did I mention the hood looking guy in the suit standing near the kitchen the whole time texting and playing with his phone? Nope, not going back nor recommending this spot.

text: Lots of stars from other Yelpers, but I didn't really think it was all that special. Came here for lunch with a coworker after checking out the menu. We arrived before the lunch rush, but it still took quite a while for our lunch to be served. I won't ding them for that... but I wish the food was better. The paella wasn't anything special - some chunks of chicken, some chorizo, and not much flavor beyond that. It seemed like they baked the whole thing in the little dish afterwards because there was a nice rice crust on one end - but that didn't make up for the blandness =/ The croquetas weren't all that great, either. Kinda hard to mess up fried foods, but they somehow managed to do that here. The croquetas were filled with a glue-like substance that I had to have with ketchup 'cause there wasn't enough flavor. Boo! My coworker admitted that the lamb grinder wasn't anything special, "Just like a French Dip..." The chorizo we shared was okay... but I think I've had better chorizo elsewhere - this one just tasted like a hot dog =/ The bill came to about $30 for two people... FOR LUNCH... mehhhhhh Will I come back? Probably not... sorry guys. GUY FIERI FAIL!!!

text: Nice hopping diner atmosphere, probably less so than the one downtown on Chapala, which I don't go to because the crowds annoy me. I hate waiting for a table! In a word, ubiquitous. PreviousIy have never really had any gripes about Cajun Kitchen. The food is fairly solid. Good ol' diner-style hash browns with nice potato flavor, moist within, crisp on the outside, which Hubs likes to order "extra crispy." Scrambled eggs okay, but smallish portions, which make me think, come on, how cheap are eggs?! And my friend Dee enjoys the chicken-fried steak with gravy. CAUTION however: the last time I ate there, a few weeks ago, I noticed on their specials board, eggs Benedict with CRAB CAKES!! Bear in mind I am not a Benedict gal, so maybe I'm coming from a place of ignorance, but the eggs were poached a little too hard, the sauce was not buttery, lemony goodness, but just weird and chemically, as though prepared from a package. Worst of all, the crab cakes were not fresh Dungeness but some disgusting crap out of a can, and there was no disguising their bitter, canned flavor as well as their mushy, runny texture. I was disgusted, and couldn't believe the cooks were not embarrassed to be serving such a mess. If you're going to charge a premium for seafood, show us the goods. Please don't insult us with food the likes of which is served to residents of some sad old-folks home where even they would rather languish in their wheelchairs than eat the mush sitting on their plates.

text: I have been to this Crackers about 10 times in the past 8 years. I do love to go there, but as one other person noted, the level of your satisfaction is directly related to the performer you go to see. I usually only go for A level comedians who have some national level of fame and a well developed act. You are going to see three comedians when you go. The first one is more or less the MC. They are comedians, but I am guessing they are someone who did well at an open mic night and are cheap to hire. The middle act is someone who is experienced and usually funny. Sometimes they are better than the featured comedian. After seeing the first two acts, then the featured comedian comes on and usually does a 30 to 60 minute show. My wife and I just went a month or so ago to see Kevin Pollak. He was very good but maybe a little overpriced. I guess it was fair seeing that he was a Hollywood star and we enjoyed all his stories about Hollywood people he knew. Emo Phillips was the best I have seen by far. His humor is so unique that you laughed during his entire show. I guess the secret to a fantastic experience is searching out their website and finding big name comedians who are coming in. As for the two purchase requirement, its OK. The drinks come with about 85% ice so you have to tell them no ice. The food is alright, but you sure don't go there for it. You have to feel for the wait staff. Trying to deliver your food and drink in the dark must be a real challenge but they do a great job. So go. Go once and see if you like it and if you do, you probably will go back. Once good way to tell if you comedian will be any good is to listen to Bob and Tom on the radio the week they are appearing. One down side to that is they usually use about 50% of their material in their act that they use on the radio, but the visual aspect of seeing the comedian do it is a better experience.
label: POS

text: The first haircut I received in St. Louis was crooked. I went back to the offending salon and got it cleaned up, but ugh, nobody likes having to do that. And why would I want to go back to the same people who gave me crooked hair? I didn't. And I didn't bother finding another place for almost 2 years. That's right, the thought of finding a suitable salon so paralyzed me, I went almost two years with nary a trim. It's not that I have high maintenance hair or anything. I just flat-out don't know what to do with it and honestly, I don't want a cut that requires I do much at all. No products, absolutely no flat-irons, maybe some blow-drying, but THAT'S IT. I don't have time for any of that crap, I'm eating or something. Also, I'm cheap. I cannot spend tons of money on gettin' my hair did because I'd rather spend it on good food. So, one day I was walking through the Loop and spotted V Vegaz. It's not far from home, their prices looked reasonable ($35 for shampoo, cut & style) and I obviously needed a haircut. I made an appointment with Erin, waved buh-bye to my long, straight, neglected hair and ended up with a cute, shorter cut with a slight edge to it. Hooray! That first haircut with Erin was in January and today I went back to her for my second. This is a very good sign, people. I didn't wait two years to get another 'do. And an even better sign? I already made my next follow-up appointment. Erin's good at what she does and I am happy to be in her capable, creative hands. Aside from my stylist, I really just love the atmosphere at V Vegaz. The decor is fabulous with its one black and white damask wall, other deep turquoise walls, gilded mirrors, quirky art (the mustachioed lady is my favorite) and the big ol' Scarface poster in back. I love that they offer you tea, coffee or water when you come in and that they play Nirvana, Interpol and Bob Marley. I also love the scalp massage, the friendly conversation and the fact that it doesn't break the bank to get a good 'do at V Vegaz. I am so glad I finally broke down and got a damn haircut and I'm especially glad I got it here!
label: POS

text: I went to Aki Sushi last night for a special free sushi event. The deal was that they would continuously bring you free sushi and you would buy drinks from the bar. They extended happy hour till 9pm which made for $4 wines and $5 cocktails. I also had a dish of seaweed salad in addition to the free sushi. It turned out that many more people came than were originally expected. This made for less sushi per individual. I sat at the sushi bar. The sushi wasn't pre-refrigerated or anything like that. It was all made fresh. They were giving out good quality rolls too, not just salmon and avocado. The sushi was good. They have a buffet selection on their menu for under $25. This is a good place to come and eat a ton of sushi. I can't say anything about what they are doing in the kitchen, but looking a some of the previous reviews I would say the sushi bar is the big attraction here. With Morimoto's just around the corner, this place offers a cheaper Japanese alternative where you can eat until you've had your fill. The service was very good also. All the staff were very kind and accommodating under the heavy work load. Although I ate only about 12 to 15 pieces of sushi, I left a fan of Aki just because they have an all you can eat menu. Their cocktails are really good too. 4 stars for all you can eat sushi

text: First things first: CASH ONLY. Know before you go (we didn't, but luckily there's an ATM across the street). And while I said the prices were moderate, it's easy to drop $100 on dinner if you do appetizer/entree/dessert. On to the food: delicious. We started with carrot soup. It was artfully presented with olive oil drizzled on top. It had a bit of cream and was rich and flavorful. There was a bacon/pork flavor to it. My friend loved that, but I found it overpowered the carrot flavor. I also dislike bacon, so it may have been my prejudice. Next we shared the plato de charcuteria. Manchego cheese with quince paste was a favorite, as was the cured pork tenderloin (paper-thin slices with an incredible texture). There was also serrano ham, chorizo, goat cheese, and some type of very strong blue cheese. Served with grilled bread drizzled with olive oil. For dinner my friend got the black rice with shrimp. I had a taste; it was interesting, but for the life of me I can't identify the flavors. Squid ink, perhaps. My pork tendorloin was delicious, grilled but tender inside. The highlight was the red pepper and mango 'salad' beneath it. It was warm and delicious, sweet and savory. And everything was beautiful to look at, wonderful plating. Finally, we each ordered spicy hot chocolate and a side of churros. The churros were made fresh, not too sweet, a nice complement to the chocolate. The chocolate was so rich and smooth that we used it more like a fondue for the churros. I'd like to go back and try the other chocolates. They even offer a tasting, I understand. Cafe Apamate is a BYOB, so bring your own Spanish wine for a great night out. In all, we ordered far too much food. My friend knew better and got her entree to go. We were surprised at how quickly our bill added up. More than we expected to spend on a casual weeknight with a buddy. But for a special night out it is fine. And next time we'll know to order less food. They also serve mini-tapas, which is certainly 'mini' but reasonable if you just want some light bites. Oh, and the service was friendly and attentive.

text: The only reason this place still exists is that West Philly is dying for more restaurants and is desperate enough to patrionize what we can get. I appreciate that they contracted a good deal on hops prior to the hop shortage and skyrocketing prices, but NOT enough to want it to be the primary flavor in every beer offered. They had, and ran off, atleast 2 decent brewmasters that I know of. If you want a good, local microbrew try the Philadelphia Brewing Company, Manayunk Brewery or Riverhorse Brewery. All three are amazing. PIZZA: Cutting corners seems to be their primary motivation. Times are tough but I still want a decent pizza when I am paying for one. Sparse toppings, often hastily made. Trio fries=burnt leeks. Allegro pizza doesn't have a wood fired oven and will still knock the socks off a Dock street pizza anyday. WARNING: The "VEGAN" pesto is a lie. Some of the prep-cooks put parmesan cheese in it to "make it taste better." Some of them don't, but most vegans I know aren't willing to take the chance. CUSTOMER SERVICE: I live in West Philly and am friends with several cooks and servers who used to work here. There's a reason the owner declared bankruptcy and ran atleast one other restaurant to the ground. They treat their workers like poop and the good ones leave. I can't speak for those still there. Maybe if they were paid fair wages, treated better by management, and allowed to make and serve quality food (not forced to cut every corner possible) this place would be decent. And the acoustics are AWFUL. It is hard to hear the person sitting next to you. Throw rug anyone? It could help with the cafeteria style sound. I'm just looking for a good slice and beer to wash it down. But I live 2 blocks from the place and get take-out from other places or go downtown for my pizza and beer. Its a shame, I wish they were good.

text: Do not fail to visit the Desert Museum. You'll be sorry if you leave town and then realize what you missed. This is a natural history museum that includes a zoo and aquarium. That's right, there is riparian habitat in Arizona (although much of what once was has been destroyed by humans), and you will see the plants, fish and animals that live(d) there. But the main attraction for me is the walk through the desert where you can see plants and animals in their natural setting, or close to it. If you can come here at the right season, you will see the desert in bloom, which is a magnificent sight. There is an artificial cavern which teaches about cave formation and the creatures that live in caves, as well as geology and plate tectonics. If you visit in summer, this exhibit, the reptile house, the aquarium and the riparian exhibit are shady places to hide from the sun. There is one gift shop near the entrance, but you may want to defer purchasing until you've seen the other one by the food court, especially if you're looking for clothing and jewelry items. This is one museum where there is actually a good restaurant on the premises. My server recommended the Blue Corn Pumpkin Chicken, which was excellent. I would rate the Ocotillo Grill **** for food, ** for service (it was a bit slow) and $$$ for price. Lunch daily 11-3 from October to April, and Dinner on Saturdays from June to August. Call before you go to verify opening times if dining here will be an important element of your visit. They also have the standard snack bars and food court, which are about what you'd expect (i.e. mediocre). IMPORTANT: Wear a wide-brimmed hat and use sunscreen. Even in winter you can get sunburned. There are a number of paved trails, but more are unpaved. Wear shoes that are comfortable to walk in and suitable for unpaved trails if you want to see everything.

However it was also the lunch/dining area for the staff who were happily eating and licking their fingers while preparing food. The waiters were rude and the are was unclean. The friend I went with SWORE this was amazing BBQ and I saw local awards on the wall for Best BBQ. Boy was my friend and the local paper wrong. Even thought it was lunch rush time the BBQ was dry and tough. You had to choose one of the 3 sauces to wet the meat enough to go down. I was sad to see the portion at this BBQ joint and that no sides were included in the inflated price. Never again and the hunt continues for some decent BBQ

text: First I should say that I don't have much experience with Korean food, so I am not in a good position to say whether it was a well done Korean meal. This is a very well decorated fast food Korean place. The music played was great and we really liked the atmosphere. The waiter forgot some of our meal and the food came out all at different times. Although the atmosphere held promise, we were not fans of the food. I had hoped to find some healthy options on the menu and could not. The vegetables in the rice were canned/frozen. The only non-fried rice was the curry. I thought the curry was decent. Disappointingly, the spring rolls were fried, which may be a regional way to cook spring rolls, but I sure wish the menu said as much. My young son ordered the ugly dog and loved it. What's not to love about a processed corn dog deep fried in an additional batter and then covered in sugar? I don't think I can in good conscience let him order it again. I am very happy to see more ethnic food restaurants moving into Edwardsville. But, I'm afraid this won't be a regular stop of ours.
label: NEG

text: Overall: It's a store with so-so merchandise. If you've got time to kill, and don't want to be bothered by sales people asking if you need help finding anything, why not take a stroll in Daffy's? It's just as my sister described it, "It's like Nordstroms Rack, but whack." I'm going to say that she's pretty darn accurate. If I can remember correctly, there are 8 floors, but shopping is only on floors 1,3,4 and 5 (what happened to the 2nd floor?). Each floor is separated into departments (men's, women's, accessories, etc.). Merchandise: I must have came on an "off" day for Daffy's. I was unable to find anything that I fancied. I don't like to be a label whore, but when I shop, certain brands pop more for me. On this trip to Daffy's the only brand that I recognized was Ben Sherman. The second hand store down the block that had a crazy array of designers. As for customer service: I don't think they have any. My sister and I were on three different floors and were there for about 45mins to an hour and not once were we greeted.

text: I ate at the Taproom only once, but it was enough to make me never want to return. My boyfriend and I went for lunch one day during the week and were excited at first when we entered and saw the selection of brews and the ecclectic menu. It seemed a little pricey for the informal setting, but there were definatly some interesting items offered. Our excitement began to wane after it took 25 minutes for our waitress to come take our drink/food order. That was 25 minutes when there were only two other tables occupied in the entire place and there seemed to be employees wandering aimlessly or standing unhelping-ly still at the empty bar. When we finally did get to order, the drink special of the day we wanted, which was advertised on signs in multiple places in the restaurant, was mysteriously out (at 11:00 am already?) and no attempt was made to alter any of the signs nor was an alternative offered to us. My boyfriend ordered a blue cheese burger cooked medium with roasted potatoes and I ordered a pork loin sandwich with mashed potatoes. We tried to order relatively simple fare because we were restricted on time. It took us almost 40 minutes to receive our food. Since when does a burger and a sandwich take that long to cook? Not only that, but tables that ordered after us received their food before us. The burger was overcooked to the point of being inedible and the roasted potatoes were served cold. My pork loin sandwich was very good so I ended up sharing my lunch with my boyfriend so he wouldn't go hungry. We asked the waitress to take back the burger and take it off our bill and she acted like nobody has ever had the audacity to request such a thing before. It actually took her two tries to get the bill right and she acted haughty and unfriendly the whole time. If we hadn't been running late from our lunch disaster I would've requested an intense meeting with the manager. Needless to say she did not receive a tip. I could've just gone on a bad day, this place seems to have potential, but unfortunatly with the staffing and operational issues it ended up being a huge headache. And with an overpriced menu of items that can mostly be found at other local establishments like Cabana, Jackson's, Bosco's or Noshville there doesn't seem to be much of a reason for me to give it another go.
label: NEG

text: Bongo Java is a great place to hang out, study, smoke a cigarette and enjoy a great cup of coffee. When I say great cup of coffee, I don't just mean that by my own personal taste. When coffee is evaluated, it's given something called a "cupping score". The perfect cupping score is 100 and most great coffee is a 90 or 85. Bongo scored a 95. Not to mention, the price is great! It's a lot cheaper than Starbucks and they have just as many frilly drinks on the menu. There can be a long wait at the busy points of the day when music industry people and Belmont students line up to try and grab a cup of coffee before the next meeting or class. Once you get your coffee, you can enjoy it outside on the fantastic wooden porch and enjoy Belmont Blvd or inside and enjoy the local art that's hung on the walls. Bongo is home to a lot of Nashville artwork. Every few months the paintings on the walls change to showcase another local artist. Even the tables inside were painted by local artists. Besides coffee and a great hang-out spot, Bongo has a little theater upstairs. It's small and quaint. Unplugged shows, stage play readings, etc. are held there on the weekends and sometimes throughout the week. Bongo is easily my favorite cafe in Nashville.
label: POS

text: I got a Groupon for this bakery and decided to try it out. I'm a total sugar and chocolate addict and always looking for a great bakery, something other than the thousand Italian bakeries that seem to abound in the Philly area. I bought 4 items on my first trip (and all within the limits of my $10 Groupon!) I got a specialty pastry called a "marjolaine," a chocolate/chocolate cupcake, a hazelnut cake slice, and a complimentary double chocolate brownie-cookie drop with vanilla glaze (because I actually came a little under the $10 and they wanted to make up for it.) Very friendly service from the one woman I dealt with on a Thursday afternoon. I ate the cookie first. Very "meh." It was dry except for the embedded chocolate chips. You can make much better at home using the Baker's Chocolate Drops recipe found on the back of their unsweetened baking chocolate, very easy to do, just add a generic confectioners glaze. Next I tried their specialty marjolaine, priced at $4.99, so I expected it to be good. This is a four layer hazelnut meringue filled with hazelnut and chocolate cream, a bit of jam, and covered with a chocolate glaze. Again, I was underwhelmed and had a hard time pinpointing why. Ultimately, I found it to be too rich and too sweet (half a slice made me sick to my stomach) but without a whole lot of actual flavor. The chocolate glaze quality was pretty good though. Next I tried the cupcake. And I found myself asking, what do the following have in common: 1. Sahara 2. Mohave 3. Death Valley 4. This cupcake You guessed it - dry dry dry! And the frosting was airy nothingness. I threw part of it away. Why do people bother to make cupcakes that aren't moist yumminess? If you want cupcakes, go to Brown Betty. End of story. Finally, the hazelnut cake square. Again, a lot of airy sweet nothingness, very unsatisfying. (In fact, the bakery box, when it held just the cupcake and cake square, weighed almost nothing. The marjolaine was the only hefty pastry.) This place reminds me of many of the local Italian bakeries, because their cakes tend to be a lot of airy sweetness as well. I was hoping for something different given the "Swiss" designation. No such luck. I won't be coming back.
label: NEG

text: I must say I wasn't enthused about venturing to this place due to the mediocre reviews, but my coworker Karyn S. said their salmon is "amazing". So I knew I had to give it a chance. We drove down Lindbergh in Karyn's bright red Jetta bumping to country music! We quickly arrived at Plaza Frontenac about 5 minutes later. We were immediately seated and introduced to our waiter. Now, Canyon Cafe has a lot of unique offerings that have set them apart from any other "tex-mex" restaurant I've been to. For starters they bring out a basket of chips which consist of 3 different flavors but I at the moment I can only remember two of the flavors (sweet potatoe and wonton). The wonton chip is "Amazing" that was definitely my fav and there were only two wonton chips in the whole basket! Moving on to the entrees...They had a special of the day which was BBQ salmon with mashed potatoes and vegetables. I am a BBQ girl so that is what I went with. Ade w. ordered what I was originally going to order the pecan salmon with sweet mashed potatoes Karyn S ordered the fish tacos with black beans. Look at the pics I posted the presentation for the fish tacos was amazing. The taco shell was orange on the outside and black in the inside....a beautiful contrast of colors! Then for dessert they bring out a piece of chocolate actually im not sure what it is...but its in the husk. It's like a little treat. They definitely have trademarks that set them apart. The price I didn't like so much at $14.95, It's not a place that I can frequent for lunch weekly only on special occasions. The food took awhile to come out so make sure you have time ie an hour and a half..so your manager won't yell at you for coming back late. Other than that I don't have any other complaints. Don't be discouraged by all the not so great reviews...give it a shot..and decide for yourself! I had a great time!

text: I would actually give this place 4.5 stars. I've been here twice, once for regular dinner and another time for the suckling pig. I had to put my credit card down for the whole pig and there is a cancellation penalty. You also need to reserve it 72 hours ahead, I believe. It was amazing. I came with 5 other people and it left us all stuffed. The pig comes with several sides--fingerling potatoes, grilled green onions, rice and beans, etc. The chef came out like they do in peking duck restaurants and he cut up the pig just the way we wanted it. We also got to try the brain, cheeks, and other parts that may make some people squeamish. The drinks here are just ok (e.g., I've had the sangria which is neither delicious nor strong.) The service is fine but they're usually so packed and busy that it's hard to get your server's attention since the place is so big. The bar is more like a waiting area for small parties and it's not a comfortable place to eat or drink. The flatbread pizzas are good and my favorite appetizer is the aged manchego cheese with apple slices and truffled lavender honey. The honey goes amazingly with the cheese and apple to taste like something I've never found anywhere else! I'd love to go back and try the paella. As for the decor, it's an interesting place. There is one seating area that has white curtains while there are regular tables and chairs to the side. There is another dining area near the bar which is more like a high table with benches. The food is great so make sure to make an opentable reservation a few weeks in advance!
label: POS

text: We have heard so much about this place from friends that live there, that when we got the opportunity to join a bunch of our friends there, we jumped at the chance. We went there on a Sunday with a whole crowd of about 75 people for brunch. This had been pre-arranged by our friends down there, and the TBBC was gracious enough to open up at 11am so a bunch of hung over goths from around the world could enjoy what our organizers do at least once a week. The atmosphere was just as we expected - a pub. But the big tanks and the beer selection were impressive. The menu looked great. We took a seat and waited for our server. This is when things went wrong. It took 20 minutes to get a server to even look our direction. When we did, he commented on how he wasn't far behind us in the hung over department. We're cool and all, but that wasn't real professional buddy. We watched as all of the other tables got served drinks and food and we patiently waited, knowing that getting inundated with a huge rush like that had to be difficult. People who got seated after us got served faster than we did. We finally got to order, and waited. 15 minutes for the drinks, and over half an hour for half of our appetizers to come. Those appetizers arrived approximately 1 hour after we arrived. We looked around, and we were the only table that had not gotten food. The rest of our appetizers(which they were out of, so we had to order different ones) came after our food, once we got it an hour and 20 minutes after we got there. The six of us at our table commented that we felt like we were in an episode of Hell's kitchen. Our wait staff was disorganized, and I can only assume that the kitchen was as well. No one's orders were coming out at the same time - there were people who got their appetizers at the same time others were getting their entrees. I understand that we created a huge demand all at once, and the manager was very accommodating when I spoke to him about our experience, but it makes me question how they run on a normal busy weekend night. I want to give them another try, because the food was good when we finally got it, and I do realize that these were special circumstances. I want to give them more stars because I do feel for them, but I just can't based on the service. I'll go again, and hopefully they'll make up for it then.

text: Very disappointing and pricey. I went to Baru with high hopes and I was pretty disappointed. My partner and I ordered 3 tapas: the mazorca, the ceviche, and the calamari, all on our server's recommendation. The mazorca (a kind of corn salad) was tasty but totally seemed like something I would throw together while drunk (corn, feta cheese, mayo, and crushed potato chips). The ceviche was very bland and the calamari was heavy, very chewy and as salty as a snack food. The tapas are 8-10 bucks a plate and I thought the portions were tiny. As an entree we split the fried fish of the day which was the highlight. For a place that is BYOB, our meal was still $90 bucks. Also we sat outside, which means about 3 feet from Magazine Street, so it was noisy. Overall, I thought the food was overpriced and needed some more attention. text: The Old Courthouse is one of the most historically significant buildings in St. Louis. Here is where Dred Scott sued and won freedom from slavery for himself and his wife, a ruling that was ultimately overturned by the Supreme Court and was one of many leading factors to the Civil War. While it was a place where slaves were auctioned, St. Louisans can feel good in that the Old Courthouse was one of the first places that ruled against slavery. Today it is a wonderful landmark that features tours to young and old. Admission is free, and there is much to see. The building is gorgeous and offers many shutterbugs plenty of opportunities for picture taking. There are also fun dioramas to look at that depict the history of the Courthouse. Everyone should make the trip to the Courthouse at least once just to understand the importance of the city through the ages. The Arch is within walking distance, and features a shop at its base. A long elevator ride creaks up to the top of the Arch for a stunning look at the beautiful city. Those who are claustrophobic may want to skip the trip to the top, as the elevator cars are extremely tiny. One cool aspect of the Arch is that it sways in the wind, which will always give you a bit of a thrill! While Old Courthouse tours are free, the Arch is not. Prices depend on age [$7 and under] and the wait can be lengthy.

text: The Venture Inn has been a tradition in the somewhat seedy world of the Gay-borhood of Philadelphia. With more and open acceptance of different life styles, however, new, upscale, expensive and even outstanding eateries have popped up all over the place in the Washington Square area that cater to mainly a gay clientele, and therefore some of the old places have been left behind. The Venture is one of them. Although a "grand dame" of the community, it nonetheless has been left behind and nowadays caters to mainly an adult community, from which the moniker "The Denture Inn" has emerged. Although unjust, its reputation continues despite new management and what seems to be an honest effort at changing its character. The small side street where Venture is Camac Street, one of the numerous alley-type streets all over the older part of Philadelphia. These small streets have become more pricey and upscale, however, Camac has maintained a sort of seedy reputation due to its commercial employment. We went to the Venture Inn just to see how things had changed. I'm afraid they haven't sufficiently to go there again. In four categories, service, food, ambiance, and price, it loses to the neighboring establishments. First the service. Our waiter was obviously used to the older crowd and seemed to want to be our friend from the start. Frankly, if I wanted to be friends with a waiter, I'd make it outside of a restaurant. His overtures seemed pedantic, especially compared to the mediocre service we got which included forgetting a round of drinks we ordered with dinner. Second, the food. The mussels I ordered came in a tasty sauce. However, there were several unopened, bad ones. That is something any good restaurant would be able to screen. The food was generally good, although the presentation was "homey", not what you would expect for the price. No espresso. Third, the ambiance. On a beautiful cool summer evening in Philadelphia, al fresco seating would have been a plus. The Venture Inn restaurant sits in a building where the smoke stench has permeated the walls over decades and decades. The yellowish walls attest to the nicotine and tar of the pre-smoke prohibition in Philadelphia. Frankly, I was gasping for breath after an hour. Fourth, the price. We spent forty per person including a glass of wine each. Right around the corner, I can get the same at an upscale, new, saucy Mixto restaurant that features Cuban/Colombian infusion with knock-your-socks off service and outstanding ambiance and food. It is obvious by the clientele surrounding us that the Venture is happily within its core clientele of tired gay men in their 60s to whom a disrespectful out-of-shape waiter and mediocre food is a compliment.

text: I went here for brunch on a Sunday expecting large crowds as the weather is spring-y for the first time in months. When I arrived around 1pm, P&K was solid, but not busy (empty booths and not much of a waiting line, just 2 small parties ahead of me about to be seated). Note: I have been here multiple times previously at night for drinks and light fare and found it a decent time, beers are a bit overpriced but aren't they all these days. Music: Was stale, few year old alternative soft rock of the worst variety... the Killers, Keane, Deathcab... just... old. But appropriate me thinks for the clientele (that comes next). If it was a staff member's iPod then they need their music privileges revoked. Not only was it inappropriate music for a Sunday brunch, but inappropriate for a bar with such a great decor. Patrons: Belong in Manayunk, not center city. Guys covered in nothing but popped collar polos and sandals with shorts... are we serious? And of course the experience isn't complete without a compliment of drunk post-sorority women (mid to late 20s) being self important and yelling at each other about Macy's and god knows what else. Staff: Young, bright and very friendly, but apparently inept at their jobs. The hostess forgot to seat me, the bartender forgot to get my beer, and between those two and a waitress, they had quite a bit of trouble helping someone else purchase a simple gift card, bouncing him back and fourth between each other until they finally were able to tag-team him out the door. The hostess told me there was a party ahead of me and I would have to wait one moment for a table. No problem, I let her know I would sit at the end of the bar (closest to the door) to wait. She managed to forget I was there until I was able to make eye contact as she peeked in the door at one point. She was apologetic and I appreciated it, instead of her trying to play it off, gold star right there. Also, while at the bar, the bartender managed to take my beer order, but then forgot to actually get it for me until she walked by two or three more times with a 'oh'. My server was pleasant, but took long in every action he performed (giving a menu, taking my order, clearing my table, getting my check). Which would make sense if it was busy... alas, I was one of only a few diners seated in his area - there were at least 4 open tables in my eye sight. Food: I ordered the "breakfast americana" ($10), or whatever trite name they came up with for two eggs with bacon, toast and potatoes. The portion was underwhelming for brunch fare to begin with and to add insult to injury, they managed to break one of my over easy egg yolks and instead of replacing it, decided to serve it after overcooking the yolk so it was gummy. I assume this was done so it wouldn't be noticeable to the expediter. So, on to the eating bit: out of the two eggs, one was edible and at that task it managed to be under seasoned and bland even though there were flecks of herbs atop. Good start. The potatoes were covered in a reddish grease(paprika? it didn't taste like anything so would make sense) and were severely undercooked to the point of crunchy, not even a bit of crispy skin on the outside of a single one. However, the perhaps 10 pieces of bacon that accompanied the 1/2 cup of potatoes, two medium eggs and two 1/8 inch slices of white bread toast (with a big dollop of butter laid on them) were slightly overkill (rolls eyes), but obviously they know their strengths as it was cooked well, and had a decent taste (not overly salty). I did mention the cracker thin pieces of toast right? ok, whew. I can't stress how poorly executed this food was, and this at 1pm after a few hours of brunch service already? If you can not make a simple over-easy egg correctly I doubt you can do much else right either. Summary: "Yo bro, wanna grab some brewskis and grub?" Unless this statement would cause you to high five your 'brother' in glee then, no. Look elsewhere for a much better meal on a gorgeously weathered day... the city has so much to offer in respect to brunch fare and a better class of patrons, for you to settle for Pub and Kitchen is a travesty worse than being served $10 gummy yolks. Stick to beer and burgers after dark. Note: I signed up for Yelp just to post this review, I hope it was as good for you as it was for me.

text: I honestly don't get the popularity of the Creperie. I mean there are real French restaurants in the city. They don't even serve crepes at all. They serve galletes (though probably not made with buckwheat). A crepe should be a light delicate thin pancake with an eggy taste, not the heavy bland things they turn out. You should be able to enjoy a crepe on its own without a filling. On that topic, their savoury fillings are the Chef Boyardee version of the real thing - the sauces too thick and salty instead of light and herby. In fact, all you taste is salt, from the onion soup to the St. Jacques and Bourguignon, even the Florentine (mmm salty spinach). Maybe it appeals like the Pirates of the Carribean ride in Disneyland. I mean the decor is same, fake stone and dungeon like niches with staff in French waiter costumes instead of Pirate garb. It relies on a sense of suspension of disbelief. Yes, this is a real French crepe; I'm in a pirate cave and not Orange County. The low light probably helps in the same way; you can't actually see the reality. What the Olive Garden does for Italian food, the Creperie does for French. The most obvious sign of this is that the menu does not change. A real French restaurant, strike that, a real restaurant will change it's menu to take advantage of seasonal fresh ingredients. But the Creperie is serving that same thing day in and day out for decades. Go to a chain for that kind of food, it costs less. This is a really popular place, but I don't get it. The service is attentive, friendly and efficient, but the point of going to a restaurant is to eat. It's not that the food is inedible, it's just not near authentic nor worth what they charge for it. I guess people will pay for the illusion sometimes and ignore the substance.

The counter person asked for my order and I chose the Jerk Chicken with Cabbage and Plantains. There was another customer who was probably a regular named Les who ordered the same thing. She asked me what part of the chicken I wanted, breast or leg? I replied "the breast", she asked the same question to Les and he replied "I'll take a breast and a leg, when a mon wakes up in the morning with a leg in his hand and a breast in his mouth he's a lucky mon" Can't argue with him-can you?
