text: Ew. No. NO. 1904 Beerhouse is located inside of River City Casino. They have a pretty wide variety of food. So obviously you know I don't like this place, since I gave it one star. But because I'm trying to be at least a LITTLE bit nice, I'll start with the positives. The place is beautifully decorated. There's a definite German theme. Even the waitresses are dressed like barmaids. It's actually kind of cool. Our waitress was very sweet. She explained everything on the menu to us to the best of her ability, and she even brought us samples of beer that we weren't sure about. Another plus? They have a LOT of beers on tap. The day I went, they had about thirty beers on tap. So that's pretty awesome. Okay, enough of the positives. Lets get down to business. Since they were out of the Kobe Beef Corn Dogs (at noon?!?! Oookay...) we started out with the Crispy Dungeness Crab Fritters. It was like a beer battered crab cake. It was pretty tasty, and the chipotle tartar sauce that came with it was alright. The side of cole slaw was DISGUSTING, though. It was vinegar based, which I usually like, but something tasted way off about it. It was really sour. For the main entree, I settled with the Big and Cheesy Chicken Sandwich. The menu described it as 'crispy thigh chicken, sweet and spicy onions, extra sharp cheddar cheese, St. Louis style BBQ sauce on an onion roll'. Pretty tasty, right? Well, it sounded appetizing to me. Well, it came out, and it was TERRIBLE. First of all, there were way too many slimy onions on the sandwich. I removed those immediately. What was left was a rectangular block of fried chicken on a bun. Hmm. 'Where's my cheese?', I wondered. I bit into the sandwich, and quickly figured out that the cheese was STUFFED into the chicken. It was the most disgusting thing I've bitten into in quite some time. The cheese just oozed out. And there was way too much of it. Oh, and is 'St. Louis style BBQ sauce' really ketchup? Because that's what it tasted like. Ugh. I could only suffer through two bites of the sandwich before I decided I had had enough. The fries were laughable. They looked like McDonald's fries, and tasted like they had been sitting out for a while. Not hot, not crispy, just blah. My mom ordered the pizza, and it was not bad. It tasted like the kind you can get frozen from the grocery store, but whatever. She seemed to like it okay. My sister ordered the basket of fried chicken, which might have been palatable had it not come with three pieces of thigh meat. Maybe something like that should have been mentioned in the menu. She sent that back and went with the ribs, which were decent. Would I come back here? No. Not in a million years. It just wasn't very good, and even though our waitress was nice, it didn't make up for the unbearably slow service.
label: NEG

text: I was scanning through the Yelp App and I noticed a friend had checked into this Shell. The good news is that they no longer issue brake tags, according to the City website. So I walked in, politely waited for the employees to finish their personal conversations, then asked to get a brake tag. I've got to say that I don't miss the high level of customer service and the personal attention that you get at some establishments in New Orleans. The brake tagger came out and said my car was pointed in the wrong direction. I quickly spun the car to the proper orientation. By this time, a line 4-cars deep had formed. The brake tagger told me this was insufficient. Actually, she screamed it at me. That I would have to leave and get behind the other cars who came after me. I asked her what her name was and she was all to happy to yell at me and tell me to leave. I left. My subsequent eternal boycott of City Park Shell was about the only justice I would get. The complaint I registered with Shell corporate came back with the standard "we don't actually own any gas stations, they are independently owned and operated." Uh huh. text: I didn't know that they hired magicians for waiters because ours managed to disappear many times. Our work crew has gone here twice for lunch. Obtaining said magic ketchup required the manager on her obligatory 1/2 hearted "How is everything?" dance for us all to ask in a chorus of ketchupless voices "Ketchup?!" She sprung into action and low and behold 10 minutes and 1/2 of my fries choked down with nothing to prevent the salty fries from scratching my esophagus on the long journey to my belly, i got my ketchup. It's funny because when I was a waiter we used to (gasp!) keep the ketchup in bottles and leave it behind the bar for when customers ordered. Heck, they didn't even have to ask for it if ya can buy that. My signature Maguire burger was the most unoriginal patty on a small bun with a drop of BBQ sauce. I also had to remove the onions that I expressly did not order. I hate raw onions! Five of us at $71 plus tip (Yes I still tip even with this farce of a delivery because I was a waiter and a bartender for 7+ years.) Next time I'll stick to the foreign guy in the Lansdale Septa station. He always has ketchup and he can't disappear because he works in a booth. Finally I wish Yelp offered an Option of "Nothing" in the Good For: section of my review because that is what MM's is Good For: Nothing.

text: In the recent past my boyfriend and I have experienced some discrepancy in price point and our dining experience (mostly in upscale eateries). We were tired of shelling out a substantial sum of money for subpar experiences; including less than memorable food as well as floundered service. For Valentine's day weekend, I had a bit of anxiety trying to choose a restaurant that would not disappoint. Fortunately for us, Fond hit the mark on every account. We could not argue with such reasonable pricing, especially on Valentines day weekend where most restaurants take it upon themselves to skyrocket prices. John and I love variety in our meals and the pricing gave us flexibility to try more on the menu. The food was fantastic from beginning to end! We were most pleased with our entrees. I ordered the tender short rib and John ordered the pork belly, which was the perfect medley of texture, flavor, and portion. (I hate going to upscale restaurants, paying a generous bill and leaving hungry!) The sweet potatoes and the escarole were lovely complements to the dish. And though it was our second time having pork prepared with a crispy skin, #2 was just as gratifying as the first. A+ desserts! We had the cream parfait and a chocolate mousse (the first two on the menu) They were the perfect blend of flavors. Our server hit the mark when he described the first as an inside out creamsicle. The second was decadent but not overwhelming. A gentleman next to us raved over his cheesecake, listing it in his top 3 favorite cheesecakes of all time! Haha -- something we will have to try when we return. Two thing I would like to mention about the crew running the restaurant. The first is how wonderful it was to have a well versed serving staff without the pretense and formalities. Steve was friendly, down to earth and serendipitously became an integral part of our wonderful dinner. John and I celebrated my 30th at La Croix and had a terrible evening because our server could care less to give us the time of the day. Although the food was excellent, the way were were treated left a sour taste in my mouth for the past month. We came to share our experience with Steve and it turned out that he and another server knew exactly who we were talking about and shared our sentiment! Somehow, having someone else understand what kind of a jack ass we had to deal with redeemed our experience. The second thing I wanted to mention was the kinship in the restaurant. To the best of my knowledge it seemed as though many of the staff worked together before and we felt this added warmth to the atmosphere. I'm not sure if I am assuming correctly, but it seemed as though Fond was a collaboration of friends who shared the same passion and philosophy of food, put their heads together and created this terrific place. We thoroughly enjoyed our experience at Fond and look forward to going back again!
label: POS

text: What I like about the Cantina is the creativity in their burritos. To me, the reality of tacos and burritos is simply meat, maybe some beans, onions and cilantro, and a tortilla. It's available in many places. Some are better than others, and that is another story and another review. The Cantina takes those basic components and adds their embellishments without the pomp and circumstance. The asada now has a chipotle sauce, the carnitas has been simmered in salsa. Today I had the Baja Grill burrito, with regular carnitas. My friend had the Azteca (the beef steak with chipotle). Both were great. Price was acceptable. About $7.50 each. Seems on par with similar businesses of the area. Size wise it's brilliant if you love a gut buster, or it's another meal for later if you don't. I am glad I got my food to go - the tv sports is often a mood killer for me and there was plenty of that action going on. However, just to be clear: 2 stars for the breakfast burrito. I will attribute this rating to the following conditions: I finished college many years ago, I don't need cheap food, I don't need fast food, and I'm not drunk. These qualities, especially the latter one, seem to play a large role in one's enjoyment of the breakfast burrito. The breakfast burrito is different than the standare fare, but that does not make it better. I've had them twice, sober, and having been sober the night before. No burrito goggling here. The potatoes had the consistency of mashed potatoes, but more watery. The rice did nothing for me. I wondered if I visited them, twice, on off days. But when comparing notes with other food friends who went on their own time they expressed being underwhelmed as well. So, I guess you should enjoy this breakfast burrito while you're still a student and eager to over-imbibe.
label: POS

text: I have never had a good experienced at Demo's and I've tried it three times now! Reservations don't mean anything... you'll always wait (sometimes for 30+ minutes), Service is a foreign word at this restaurant, I've had bad bartenders, horrible service, and downright rude managers I say avoid this crappy restaurant at all costs! Most of the time there are redeeming qualities... ie: great service/crappy food, crappy food/great service, etc... but Demo's has NONE! Their food is lousy, the drink list is unimpressive and as I've already mentioned their incredibly poor service. After waiting 45 minutes for our reservation, without getting waited on while sitting at the bar, only to wait 25 minutes for a server of any kind to come to our table and take our drink order, who then bolted, literally jogged away before we could ALSO put in our food order (I mean, we'd had waited long enough to make our entire drink & meal selection). We didn't see the server again for another 10 minutes... and still didn't have drinks (and we all just ordered wine, no complicated mixing or anything required). After putting in our food order and waiting another 30 or so minutes we were treated to overcooked food that was tasteless and just plain not great. This particular visit inspired me to ask for a manager... and since our server wouldn't get one... I had to literally ask around to find him myself. He was also unhelpful and made it seem like we were a couple of young girls who wanted a free meal... which was NOT the case. Despite him taking off 1 of our meals for our "trouble", I insisted that I pay for it.... letting him know I would be writing a review on Yelp about my experience and I want to pay for this horrendous meal just to prove a point... I wasn't trying to get something free I was trying to have a good meal downtown with my friends and I'd rather just pay and let others know about it... so my fellow Yelpers don't waste their money. I do not recommend Demo's, in fact, I'd steer clear of Demo's at all cost. If you got a Demo's gift card... re-gift it. Trust me!

text: After three generations of serving Louisiana's finest seafood cuisine, Anthony and Gail Uglesich sadly hang up their hats and decide to close this lunch-only cash-only culinary mecca in the Garden District. When i had lived in New Orleans i was fortunate to make it to U's twice and each time was in sheer heaven! The first time I indulged here I was with my brother who is a total foodie, we launched ourselves head first into the fresh live oysters that still had their siphon reflex in-tact and could squirt seawater at you if poked appropriately. Making sure we were well hydrated with their specialty bloody Mary's; we followed up with the barbecued shrimp and barbecued oysters. Uglesich's is a place where Cajun-creole staples like jambalaya; shrimp and grits in a creamy sauce; crawfish maque choux (crawfish smothered with white corn, tomato and seasonings; blow the competition out of the water! I still dream of being served the BBQ shrimp followed by the deeply flavored and fried green tomatoes topped with shrimp and remoulade sauce. It's no surprise why limos regularly pull-up outside this divey and decrepit seafood shack and the wait for a spot in their 12 capacity establishment. Although they may not have reopened i hear since the release of their newest cookbook they have been doing some catering events for special occasions. "The Uglesich's Restaurant Cookbook," from Pelican publishers has 19 restaurant recipes that weren't in the first book, 41 recipes made in the Uglesich family home and a handful of desserts. The new book also has a nostalgic sections of photos of locals dining.
label: POS

text: I have flown through a lot of airports around the world, and this one is definitely one of the worst. Let's start with accessibility. The airport is not located in New Orleans, but Kenner, a distant suburb. Access from Interstate 10 is somewhat convenient, but not really direct, since you must travel a few miles down an airport access road before you reach the airport. Parking is probably the biggest problem. 13 bucks a day to park in the Long Term Lot, which is almost certainly full? Me thinks not. Thinking about public transit? Hopefully, you're not traveling on the weekend, when the one bus route does not actually go into downtown New Orleans, but instead drops off in one of the sketchier neighborhoods. With regards to the airport itself, it could definitely use improvement. Yes, I got excited about the free Wi-Fi as well, until I found out that it goes in and out randomly. Don't count on it to get any work done. Food wise, when the best (and only) meal options at an airport are Sonic or Popeye's, you know that there is a problem. Cleanliness is decent beyond the security checkpoint, but once you cross into the non-secured area, especially near baggage claim, beware. The bathrooms are DISGUSTING.

text: Back when I lived near South Grand, I would go here at least a couple times a month. Eventually, however, something happened. Being as egotistical as, well, anyone else on Yelp, I like to think it was because my palate graduated and I moved on to better sushi within the City. But Bill S. may be correct in asserting that we haven't gotten any sharper, but rather Sekisui has become quite dull. To be fair, all of the non-sushi meals I've had here - particularly the chicken teriyaki - have ranged in quality from "passable" to "better than I expected". The decor is inoffensive if not a bit rudimentary as well. If you, however, are one of those Japanese restaurant enthusiasts who cares about sushi and only sushi, you might as well knock both stars off my rating because hoo boy, the stuff they serve you here is rough. The ingredients look/taste like last week's haul, the cutting is lackluster, and that's even on a good night. The rolls - and this is a *huge* pet peeve of mine - are mostly rice, oftentimes undercooked at that. If you have to come here at all, I'd recommend you leave the long slip of paper blank and just get an entree. You're welcome.

text: I had an unpleasant experience trying to have my wedding here this summer. I've been a SYR guest in the past and was drawn to the privacy and the beauty of the resort nestled between the mountains with a view of the ocean. First let me say that I only stay at 5 star resorts whenever I travel. So i am rating this resort against my experiences at other 5 star resorts. If I was rating it just on the looks of the resort, I would give it 5 star, but that's not what a 5 star resort is. A 5 star resort should be top notch on service. I give SYR service 1 star. SYR was my first pick in my wedding venue for this summer but after my experience with their management, I immediately changed my venue to the Beverly Hills Hotel (which their service was outstanding). Basically to make long story short, SYR confirmed available summer wedding dates and my now husband and I drove over 1.5 hours to take a tour of the grounds again. When I called the following day to put the deposit down for the summer wedding, they told me that they were fully committed and will not be accepting additional weddings for the summer. This news came from the same person who gave me a tour, the day before and told me there were many open summer wedding dates. I insisted on speaking with the general manager, Mr, McManus, and he just told me they are undergoing management changes and were fully committed and will not be taking additional weddings for the remaining of the year. After I complained to the top executives of Rosewood Hotel (SYR is managed by this hotel group), then Mr. McManus offered us a few possible summer wedding dates. The irony of this is, when my brother and my friend called later that week, they confirmed available summer wedding dates. Obviously, we chose another wedding venue but this experience left a sour taste in our mouth and my husband and I vowed to never go there again.

I.e., a "front" business? Well, welcome to Queen Village Pizza, where they've been in business for years, where a group of middle-aged Middle Eastern men are almost always sitting out front shooting suspicious, somewhat antagonistic glares at anyone who happens to stroll by too closely, where one almost never, ever sees anyone ever actually BUYING anything there ever, and if one does actually go in and order something, one gets the distinct impression that the "staff" have to quickly remind themselves of how to construct a hoagie... like it's been a good long while since they were last asked to do it. text: Almost the textbook definition of a mediocre upscale restaurant, and sadly the go-to "elegant" spot in Boise. My totally unimaginative pork chop was served on a bed of white beans that probably had another 10 minutes of boiling before they were done. In my world, undercooking the beans is a big problem for a restaurant of any kind, least of all one like Berryhill, where the entrées are upwards of $20. The tomato bisque was totally flat (not enough cream?), and the desserts were functional at best. At least they try to locally source their meat. Add on top of everything else some live piano muzak (never a good idea) and iffy service, and there's not much to recommend -- call ahead at the Red Feather or Le Coq Rouge instead if you're looking for a nice meal.

text: Nowhere in town will you find a coffee shop cooler than Kaldi's. Not even the other Kaldi's locations that have popped up in such places as Kirkwood and downtown Clayton. Accept no substitute (and really, they don't even come close). This is the one that started it all. The coffee shop by which all other coffee shops should be judged. The original Kaldi's in the cozy Demun neighborhood is like a bastion of goodness. Maybe that's just because I hate commercialism. I hate coffee shops that are just mirror images of each other (though I won't lie and say I don't go to "those" shops in a pinch-like at the airport when I need a jolt of energy). If I can avoid chains, I will, by all means. After all, I'm the girl who wore pants to my elementary school graduation when all the other girls wore dresses. I'm a rebel, darnit. I am a bit of a hippie, too. I love walking barefoot through the park in my flowing pink skirt. I love eating vegetables and listening to the Indigo Girls. I love sitting on a blanket and eating my veggie burger with Vermont cheddar (an old staple of Kaldi's which is sadly off the menu). I love herbal iced tea and homemade blueberry pie. Their Mediterranean salad with housemade tahini yogurt dressing and thick as paste hummus seasoned with a kick of chile are to die for. Goodness lies here. The outdoor seating area is peaceful, and makes you feel as if you're in northern Cali which, to me is a good thing. I love taking beverages across the street to Concordia Seminary's grassy knoll. Sometimes I even bring a frisbee so my friends can laugh at me. It's all there. Kaldi's has a formula no other shop can replicate. It's part intellectual, part artsy, part liberal, part quinoa-scented...part perfect.

text: As a Marriott Platinum guy (81 nights in Marriotts this year!), I'm probably a hotel manager's worst nightmare. It's not that I'm unrealistic, it's just that I expect a reasonable product. When close to a quarter of your year is in hotels, why can't it be tolerable? I am here for a few days, using Points, rather than $$$. (Checked in about 5 hours ago.) I chose the Renaissance because they're usually a little more "eclectic" than the traditional full-service Marriotts or the JW properties, and a bit more upscale than the Courtyards and other members of the Marriott family. Usually a more funky design, frequently historic, converted buildings, just quirky. There are two Renaissance hotels in New Orleans. I've previously stayed at the other, but it's a little further away from things, so I chose this one. Unfortunately, "quirky" can veer off into "tired" pretty easily, and that's the impression I get here. While the room is indeed clean, nice bathroom, linens, etc., it just feels that the property is about 5 years past a good renovation. I have a desk with a chair, and an upholstered chair for my seating pleasure! Feels like there should be some sort of a table, as well. Just seems sort of barren. The furniture is somewhat beat, the TVs are still good, ol' tubes. Even the lighting seems tired - too dim. Maybe it's the damn reliance upon CFLs? text: If some out-of-towner who's never been to our fair city gripes about it being dirty, or dangerous, or any of that oher crap that can go part and parcel with most any frickin' big city on the planet, then be sure to tell them that they are, in fact, correct, and take them straight to The Gallery as soon as their precious safe and clean feet step on the Philly asphalt. I probably don't NEED to reiterate what so many have said here, but hell, it's fun, and I want to offer my take. This is about as bad as downtown Philly gets, which to me is actually saying quite a lot. As soon as you step foot into The Gallery, you instantly feel like you need a shower. It just has that imposing grimy feel to it that you can't quite place, but you know if you held one of those groovy UV lights up in it when it was all dark, you'd see the most disgusting proof of humanity's existence splashed all over everything. Sure, there are stores like Old Navy, Burlington Coat Factory, and Kmart (see accompanying review for that turd as well), but you don't really want to go into any of them at The Gallery. All the versions of those stores at this weirdo excuse for a mall (really it seems more like the reality of some lousy urban planner's lunch that he vomited up one day) came straight from Hell. If you've ever seen the movie Jacob's Ladder, you'll instantly know what I mean. This place is just skeevy beyond belief. Of course, seeing the big mural thingy smack dab in the middle featuring Bill Cosby's likeness is well worth the free admission. Hell, if you're going to go see the Rocky statue, you may as well see the painting of Bill at The Gallery! He looks down at you and smirks, knowing that you are wading through a cesspool of the lowest common denominator of mass consumerism. The only reason I'm usually at this place is because one of the trains I take plops me off at Market East Station, which is featured in the very bowels of The Gallery. But it's actually the nicest thing there, because you know you'll be getting away from there soon when heading outbound. There's a terrible excuse for a food court down there as well, featuring such craptastic selections as Subway and Popeye's and some weird-ass Asian joints serving up smoothies and chicken wings galore. What is it with the Chinese places and chicken wings in this city? Someone needs to look that up. So just remember, take all your pals to The Gallery to scare the hell out of them and make their big city fears come true. Then escape to street level and show them all the truly great stuff there is in Philly. Although, you might not make it out of The Gallery alive yourself if you don't wear some sort of Haz-Mat suit.

text: The Buffet just opened within the last couple of weeks. My wife was bragging about it and got home early from work, so we decided to give it a shot. Just got back. My wife will no longer be bragging about this buffet which has been overhyped! And, I will never step foot in there again. Lets start with the small things: 1) We wandered around to see what they had and then decided to get plates. Where were they? About 10 feet away on a triangular table by a pole -- on the outskirts of the whole food area. Whoever thought that that was a good idea should write a formal apology to all guests. 2) Why did they put up label spots for food and then not use them? I don't like talking to people and I sure in the hell don't want to have to interact with people for something I could just read if they had gotten around to putting up the labels. Fortunately, the employees there were all nice. 3) Half the food wasn't available b/c of empty platters. "Half!" you exclaim. "Yep, when the serving platters holding the food to server are only about 6 inches longer than the plates people use to serve themselves, you'll find that it's hard to keep them stocked." Now, go to the dessert area and I'm sorry to say, but over half the stuff was -- well, replaced by empty platters. 4) The lack of offerings here is only trumped by Boomtown (which ranks the worst buffet I've been to at a casino in Reno over the last 4 years). I was appalled and delighted at the offering. You see, I have been trying to lose some weight, but the wife wanted to go to a buffet and I just can't resist when food is in front of me; however, they didn't put much out there for me to choose from, so I believe I actually ate less tonight than at any other buffet in my life. Appalling that such a statement can be made at what is billed as a great experience. 5) The ribs were dry (along w/ a number of other platters I was too scared to eat) and the white fish (not sure what is was since they didn't bother telling me on their labels), well, the white fish reminded me of what I thought the porridge from The Matrix's real world would taste like. Flavor? Oh, that took the other pill. (Matrix reference for the uninitiated). 6) Two managers kept a table in our area filled, one of which must have been high-level b/c she was wearing an evening dress -- or, maybe she was just going out to the clubs after work. They had employees running over to them, running papers, heck, running an office from that table. It was wonderful! When we went to leave, we had to walk around 3 different employees (who were right near 2 managers) and cross over the roped area just to exit. Everyone loves a little exercise after eating, right? And, it's so hard for 3 employees catering to the needs of 2 managers to get out of our way so that we can exit. I must have unrealistic expectations. Now, for the positives: 1) The design of the dining area is awesome. I felt like I walked into a trap -- look at how beautiful this place is and give us your money, then we've got you! Sucker! 2) The server rocked. Always ready and available. No complaints. Next to leaving, he was the most positive part of the experience, Well, I've figured a few things out that I thought I'd share: 1) There's a reason they only have 1 cashier station rigged up at the end of the long corridor: They're not planning on being successful. 2) They're on a very low budget. No office area (at least one that's used) for the management, little offerings, and tasteless ones at that. And, well, there was one more thing I realized: Had I stayed home and enjoyed the beer and burrito from the refrigerator, I would have been more full, with higher-quality food, and enjoyed my evening. I have a suggestion for their upper-level management: Instead of trying to have a name like the failed Unbuffet of Tahoe, try being proactive and renaming it "The Disaster". It's much more apropos.

text: I am disappointed every time I go to Laff's. I usually go a couple of months in between visits and say to myself, "OK, maybe last time was a fluke. So what if the service was miserable, and all three comedians could barely muster the intelligence to launch salvos of dick and fart jokes at the crowd? This time will be better, RIGHT?" Of course, it never is. Two item minimum: ok, I get it. That's how they make their money. Fine. Could at least one of the two items not be so mindbendingly terrible that I feel like opening a vein, though? Do not order an alcoholic drink that does not come from a bottle. It will be watered down beyond belief and slapped with a ludicrous price tag. The food (a label which I am using generously) is atrocious. They have even found a way to mess up nachos. Food is greasy, poorly cooked, often burned or messed up in creative ways. They also always seem to be out of some staple item. One night, they were out of salsa. I ordered chips and salsa, and they brought be a basket of chips with nothing else and no explanation. Another night, they had no ground beef. On yet another, they couldn't make any of their wraps because they were out of tortillas. Service is also horrendous. They pack the audience in together like sardines and employ too few waiters. You will likely wait the better part of an hour for a meal. Drinks are the same deal. One time, I only got my drink (a soda) 10ish minutes after my meal had come. The waitstaff will periodically forget about you or misplace your order. The comedians are basically bottom of the barrel, as well. Usually there is a "hungry" local MC of middling quality, followed by a veritable rogues gallery of comedians who will pontificate about their impotence, incontinence, aversion to hygiene, and inability to keep a woman (SHOCKER). Usually, on a night's bill of 3-4 comedians, one MIGHT be kind of amusing (thus, the second star). Funny sidebar - Laff's seems to loooooove comedians who make lots of gratuitous noise in the service of imitating things like airplanes, racecars, and flushing toilets. One night, when there with my girlfriend and a couple of our friends, we were watching a particularly bad comic who seemed to dig making our ears bleed with his impressions. My friend, who had been in the restroom when he came on stage, returned to the table with a shocked look on her face and disclosed that it sounded, from the toilet, as though the club was under attack by the Luftwaffe. Sadly for her, she had confused an air raid with the comic's impression of a fart. I guess the only thing that's *kind of* good about Laff's is that it's easy to get free tickets to the shows. Just sign up with the cards on the tables and you'll get a call every other month or so with a password (I shit you not) to claim your free admittance. That said, I think I'm done with Laff's for the forseeable future.

Pinnacle Peak is not only inside of Trail Dust Town, but they also have entertainers walking around most nights. The night I was there, it was a balloon guy. So, obviously, this is not one of those hoity-toity steak places, where a guy comes by to fold your napkin on your chair when you leave. This is a down-home sort of steak place. But those can still be just as good as the fancy spots. But this one isn't. In fact, the food is just awful. I mean, everything about it is just bad. You have choices between what you can get, as far as chicken, steak, fish, etc., but the steak, although bad, is still the best option, because the other stuff is just disgusting. The worst part of it is that it sucks but it's also not cheap. The "cowgirl" (the smaller steak) runs a little under $20 while the "cowboy" runs closer to $25. You'll probably go home with leftovers with the cowboy, but not much. Tucson steak, in general, sucks, but this is probably the worst one of the steak places in the city. The 2* is mainly for the kids thing. If I had kids, I would probably be at this place a few times per year, just for them. The atmosphere is well-done and the service is good. But all that really just doesn't make up for that awful, awful food.

text: Hit this spot for our lead off night for Indy 500 weekend. After reading the yelpers suggestions, I made rezez for our party of 15. Maybe its cuz I live in SoCal and have had many less than satisfactory experiences booking for large partys, I was expecting the worse, especially on the Friday night of race weekend. Well well well my little pretties, these mid-westerners really know customer service and how it is supposed to work. Tables all set up where promised (upstairs, overlooking the bandstand), reserved signs everywhere, Niki (I believe), waiting nearby to get us drinking ASAP, and very cheerful to boot. We were a disorganized lot as well; folks flying in at various times, some of us wanting to hit the sack early etc. Sooo just to make sure we were an extra pain....lets ask for a few separate checks. OMG!! This would cause most SoCal service peeps to go screaming to their managers to have these horrible customers set straight! You know what Niki did? She smiled and said NO PROBLEM. What!?! She was extremely attentive with some help from her support crew and kept the drinks and food coming. The food was above average bar food, good for soaking up the booze, but to be fair we weren't really concerned about eating as much as catching up and drinking.....a lot. In summary; the band was great, the crowd of varying ages was a typically friendly, mellow mid-western kinda group, awesome service, reasonably priced, just a great place to party. Not to be missed when in Indy.

text: My friend and I stopped in one night after a Phillies game for a beer and bite to eat. My Yuengling* and his Blue Moon were quite good, however the food was another story. The eggplant was tough and the portabella mushroom caps were like small frisbees. Presentation wise - everything looked great, but I'll probably never eat here again. On a lighter note, the bar portion of this place looks like it might be a good time. The downstairs has a small bar that looks as if it might attrack an older crowd. text: i wanted to see what all the fuss was about. here's this hot new restauarant that, a la dr. dog and not much else, is making a name for itself even outside of philly. well let's start at the beginning -- the host was, simply, a tiny douche of a man-ish thing. if you take all the negative aspects from the stereotype of the cosmopolitan gay dude, you get him. same thing if you take all bad from the archetypal bitchy hostess: unkind, unhelpful, unfriendly and uncalled for. he soured our birthday dinner from the start, unfortunately. i don't know if he's gotten a big head because the restaurant has some great press or if we were treated kind of second class because we were the only people under 25 not carrying plates. this is a problem i don't much run into in philly, but it truly pisses me off. however, our waitress was super, super enthusiastic about the food and the background of james. as great as that was to see, i didn't want an obviosuly pre-fab tale cooked up by the owners about what free spirits but serious foodies they are, having traveled here and there learning to eat this way and cook that way. just give me a sentence, tell me the customs and specials and let me soak the rest up. in any case, the food was yummy. the pasta in duck ragu was fab, with the pasta itself thin as a breath. the meat was great too, but nothing as impressive as, say, audrey calire's mushrooms. and the portions were quite large as well, everything was splitable, but there is a $2.50 spilt fee per plate. plus, there was an hour wait for our meals. all praise be to the man going 'round with the bread basket! none of the desserts looked impressive, so we left them in favor or some wine elsewhere. so, as good as the pasta was, and it was good, the place just did not give off a homey, welcoming vibe. maybe it's philly's lot to be nasty in its "we're not nyc or dc but rather stuck in the middle" insecurity. but i rarely experience such a crystallization of that like i did here. from the host-creature to the decor to the other diners -- who were the type you'd find at alfa, the type you don't want to know, the philly-yuppie plus.

text: Ever since T&T opened, there has been very little need to go to downtown Chinatown. Why walk from store to store and fight off city bums and that funky smell then I can just come here? T&T is a one-stop shopping destination for my Asian cooking needs. T&T has pretty much everything you could look for when cooking Asian. Their fish is very fresh and you can see your fish swimming around in their tanks, along with lobsters, mussels, eels and other sea animals (see pictures). The meat here is also very good- their bbq is tender and savory. They also have a good selection of fresh vegetables and fruit: whether familiar items like apples, pears, oranges , broccoli, carrots, to more exotic items like dragonfruit, Chinese pears, seaweed, and other items. I like the selection of asian spices and sauces available here, and my preferred brand of rice and noodles is also stocked here. I like the sushi section and the recently added dim-sum section. It's great how you can buy something and eat it right away. The prices here are reasonable, especially when they start discounting their items in the late afternoon to get it off their shelf (after all, sushi needs to be eaten fresh). They also have a great bakery section with an assortment of pastries and stuffed-buns, and their cake selection is very impressive and flashy. This place can get very busy during the weekends, but it is worth it coming here and finding everything in one location. It might be unfortunate for the Chinatown downtown, but this place is much closer for me, and their prices are very competitive as well.

text: For my 100th review, I thought it should be special. What's more special than my favorite meal, at my favorite restaurant, in one of my top 3 favorite cities. Manale's is famous for their BBQ shrimp. Are you thinking shrimp slathered with BBQ sauce? Well, you're wrong. BBQ shrimp are shrimp baked with the heads and shells on in a mix of butter, Worcestershire and a host of other spices. I guarantee you've never tasted anything this good (although Drago's char-broiled oysters run a close second) in your life. Served with perfect New Orleans French bread (paper thin, light crust, soft, airy bread on the inside) for sopping up the sauce, this is a New Orleans staple that was originated at Manale's. In addition to the BBQ shrimp, there are other reasons to visit this New Orleans establishment as well, like the oyster bar where I once challenged a 10 year old kid to eat a very large raw oyster. He did it so I had to as well, and I hate a large raw oyster (yet tiny ones are a gift to the world). Good stiff drinks in the bar as well as oysters to die for and shuckers who win contests. Seriously. When you go to the dining room, it's like stepping into another decade. It's got that old school Italian feeling. I expect to see Carlos Marcello surrounded by his people at a back table. OK, not really since I wouldn't know Carlos Marcello from Tony Soprano...but you get the idea. The waitresses are all of that older, steak house variety. You know the kind, weathered, hardened and not about to take any crap, but still wonderful, attentive and knowledgeable because they've been there since the joint opened. The Italian-inspired menu ranges across everything you can think of and all the New Orleans classics as well, but you know, in the end, it's all about the BBQ shrimp. And that might just be the best meal on earth.
label: POS

text: I lost my Koch's virginity today. My Koch's virginity persisted despite my roomie (Kevin S) giving it a 5 star in December. I have always biked past this place without a second glance. Granted it has an assuming exterior, but once inside you are transported back in time to a piece of West Philly history. Following a softball game victory, we ended up here on suggestion of one of our teammates. First, if you can, make sure you call in advance. My friend had the hookup and they greased the preparation so our sandwich would come in 30 minutes and not 45 minutes. The wait is pretty entertaining though. I had the counterman banter with me about my Koch virginity, the California Governor (lots of Arnie accented quotes), and kept calling for me to take samples of pastrami, garlic cheese and pickles (And as a grad student, free food is always high on my menu). Once the sandwich came, I was impressed by how much it had packed in it. The Honey Turkey club sandwich was packed with turkey, lettuce, tomatoes.....just a sandwich galore! And just like the first time, you want it again and again-same applies to Koch's in the future for me. And Koch's at least will not cost you a first or second date and blown money on flowers/chocolates etc. Just $10 bucks and you are in sandwich ecstasy.

text: I boarded my dog at Zeus' Place after reading such great reviews from various sources. My husband toured the facilities, and was informed that our dog would be given frequent walks and allowed to play in the yard during the day. As our dog is high-energy and extremely playful, we were excited by this prospect. The first time we viewed our dog on the web cam, we observed a sheet covering his door. While strange, I thought nothing of it. I repeatedly checked on him throughout the day, and each time he was inside his kennel. I understand that it is a boarding facility, and constant human interaction cannot be expected. However, as the human/fellow-dog interaction was one of Zeus' selling points, this was quite disappointing. That night, I again viewed our dog on the web cam. To my horror, he was unattended in his kennel with his pinch collar was around his neck. I was extremely upset, and emailed the facility immediately stating the potential dangers of leaving a dog unattended with a pinch collar. I received a response the following day that took no responsibility for the occurrence, and failed to even attempt an apology. I frequently checked on our dog via the web feed. Two days later, "after hours", I viewed our dog unattended wearing his pinch collar. I was livid. I again emailed, and received an insensitive reply. Once I was home, and had my dog safely in my care, I visited the Zeus Place web cam. There was my dog, still on their feed! It is safe to say, I do not recommend this establishment for boarding.
label: NEG

text: I am no expert on this whole steak and hoagie thing, but I did like what I ordered. It was called the PMC and was a steak sandwich with peppers, mushrooms, onions and marinara on a soft roll. They have a lunch special that's any sandwich, with fries and a drink for $8. The sandwich alone was $7.50, so the additional 50c for the fries and drink seemed quite the deal. My sandwich was very generous, I could only eat half. My lunch companion got a hot pastrami, ate the whole thing, and promptly had food coma for most of the afternoon. He seemed to really like it, though. What I liked about McMaster's was the simplicity of the food. Maybe that makes it more authentic? You tell me. Anyway, there was nothing done to froo-froo up the food. No avocadoes, no chipotle mayo, just solid and simple blue collar stuff. The french fries were hot and fresh, and were very similar to the kind of fries from In and Out, except bigger, if that gives you an idea of what to expect. I thought they were delicious and I'm normally loyal to the Belgian double-cook method of making fries. Service was really really good. The guy behind the counter was extremely friendly, gave honest recommendations, even admitted to eating the fries with mayo - viewed with absolute horror in the US usually - and that's how I took my fries too. Thanks, brother. He also happily pointed out the drinks were refillable and asked several times if he could top us up. One thing to keep in mind is that IV is a dead zone right now, thanks to spring break, so service might not be so hot when the hoardes of students are back. The remaining half of the sandwich became my lunch the following day and it was still good. Bonus. ps. lots of room to sit outside.

text: AVOID GUN TRADER. READ THIS BEFORE YOU GO! I can't believe the positive reviews on this site, given my personal experience and the overwhelmingly negative testimonials posted elsewhere. The other 1-star reviews below show similar experiences. The guys at this place were so bad, I set up a Yelp account just to warn others! I trusted their expertise to make an accurate recommendation on equipment. When they were wrong and I tried to make an exchange, both guys in the store were complete jerks. I took my boyfriend back with me the second time, and it was just as bad. I calmly explained to them the problems I was having with the equipment, which created serious safety concerns, and they acted as if it was all my fault and I must be wrong about what I was telling them. They offered me no solutions EVEN THOUGH THEY MADE A FAULTY RECOMMENDATION, other than to send the gear to the company. I will be doing that myself. I'd rather pay shipping than to deal with these jerks again. They have lost two "frequent flyer" customers, and we will be spreading the word. There are plenty of good options in Reno for gun stores. DON'T PATRON GUN TRADER, unless you find joy in being insulted. Instead, try any of the big sports stores, Silver State Arms, or US Firearms Academy. The last 2 are within a mile, and offer much better customer service. FOLLOW UP: It get even better. After contacting the manufacturer, they confirmed that Gun Trader had given us bad information and misrepresented proper use of the product. Manufacturer sent an email stating such, which we took to Gun Trader to try to get an exchange for the correct gear. They have a "no return" policy, but I would expect them to take responsibility for their error. They refused to read the email. It degraded into the owner straight out calling me a liar. Thanks to my chivalrous boyfriend not backing down to bullies, I got my money back. Father and son are clearly used to throwing around their immense (literally) weight, and have serious issues with being wrong. We will be calling the Better Business Bureau.

text: I took Greyhound once, and I will never take it again. I went to Ocean City, MD a few years ago with my friend for New Year's Eve (weird destination, I know, but Seacrets is actually really crowded and really fun for New Year's Eve). Anyway, she drove, and we planned on coming home the next day. However, she met a guy in Seacrets and decided to stay in Ocean City an extra day or two so that they could go out the next night, but I had to be at work after the holiday ended, so I had to get home asap. Since no trains run anywhere near Ocean City, I had no choice but to take Greyhound. Reluctantly, I got a ride to the bus stop and bought my ticket. Right off the bat, the trip took a turn for the worst, since the driver was over an hour late. The driver! Seriously. I had to sit in this tiny station in the middle of nowhere with some real weirdos an extra hour while the bus drive took his good old time showing up. Finally, we boarded the bus and headed north. Now, I know the bus makes a lot of stops (mostly at random gas stations in sketchy areas), but I then discovered that my trip would be extended further because I had to change buses not once, not twice, but THREE times. To get from MD to Philly. And, guess what? The bus driver for the second bus was also late, so I had to sit and wait in the middle of nowhere, in a station without a bathroom or a place to get food, for an undetermined amount of time (since there was no information about how late the bus driver was running), and I had no idea where I was. Great. In the end, I finally arrived in Wilmington, DE (one hour south of my home in Philly) SIX HOURS after I first got on the bus. It took roughly 3 hours to drive from my home to Ocean City. And, since the bus was running late, I got to Wilmington really, really late at night and had to call my dad to come get me because the next bus didn't leave for Philly for another 2 hours. Never, ever again am I taking the bus. The kicker of the story? It cost me about $70 for the bus ride from hell. That's almost as expensive as Amtrak. Not cool. Also, the people on Greyhounds? Not the cleanest or most normal people on earth. On one leg of the trip, I got a guy with track marks who decided to sit next to me and try to hit on me for about an hour, before he passed out and wound up falling onto me (I was squished against the window). On another leg, I got a toothless old lady who talked at me nonstop, and I had no idea what she was saying. There was also a fat guy with a shirt that didn't cover his belly who sat across from me, snored, and drooled. Plus, add in the crying children and the other colorful folks on the bus, and I hope you can imagine the 6-hour bus ride from hell that I had to endure. Like I said, never again. I'm also never going somewhere with that particular friend if she's driving. Word to the wise - never ditch your friend for a guy you meet in Seacrets on New Year's Eve. Let's just say that her date with him didn't turn out the way she hoped. The guy turned out to be a jerk.
label: NEG

text: Public Storage on McNally is a great spot not only for storage, but also for bands to rehearse and record. For about a year, my band split a storage space with a couple of other local bands, and I quickly realized we weren't the only group with that idea. Our storage space was indoors, and all throughout the hall you could hear the sounds of gospel, rock and hip hop acts rehearsing. For our carpeted space (which was about 15'x20') we paid a total of $300 a month. We were also able to leave our equipment there, knowing it would be safe and sound in the heavily locked facility. Public Storage has a gate that requires a security code for entry, and there is always someone in the front office keeping an eye on things. They have a cargo elevator and a dolly for everyone to use, and there is typically plenty of room for parking. While I used the space for band practice, I wouldn't hesitate to use it for personal storage.

text: Once you get past the obstacle course that is finding this place, you'll really enjoy time spent at Yazoo's tap room. The building used to be an old car manufacturing plant, and was subsequently abandoned before coming to house Yazoo. So, there's lots of ambience to be found in the old brick walls (there's just not lots of air conditioning for those hot summer days). While it gets crowded, you can usually find a seat in the room adjacent to the tap room, or out in the courtyard. As for ordering, get the sampler ($6 for 5 tastings) and pair it with the cheese platter. Yum. While, I'm not a big fan of all their beers, I do love trying them in rapid succession. The only problem is that they don't have any means of identifying which beers are which once they've poured them (most places use a place mat with writing on it). So, it can be hard to remember what's what. Also, be sure to get a growler - it's a relatively cheap way to enjoy a good amount of beer...I would suggest their hefeweizen or the dos perros.

text: Tang's is a great Chinese food truck at Penn. This one has long lines at lunch time as well, but it's not as bad as Yue Kee's. My favorite and just about only dish here is the Combo (add eggplants) for $4.25, which is a meatlover's dish basically. Other than that, I get the sweet and sour chicken. The combo dish has pork, beef, chicken, shrimp, carrots, and some sort of cabbage (plus eggplants for 25 cents if you want). The eggplants here are by far the best vegetable they have, so get that. The beef is definitely my least favorite of their meat. They cook their chicken in some sort of ginger broth. These guys are Vietnamese, but they do Chinese food quite well. I'm quite convinced that they order their Chinatown chicken and bbq pork from somewhere, but no matter. The food tastes good, and that's the important part. Try to get there before 12:15 or after 2PM to avoid long lines. They close at around 5PM.

text: Pros: -Great steaks (American better than Wiz here) if you get one of the good cooks who juices up the meat and doesn't let it dry out. -Open late-ish (1am on weekdays) -Good crowd control setup indoors (maximizes space) -Upstairs seating (avoid the crowd downstairs) Cons: -Stupidly long lines and wait times! -Later in the night = more and more bar crowds. -Staff. The biggest con. Most, not all, are just inefficient bordering on lazy. There are a minimum of two people who are always just standing around doing nothing. The cooks are the worse. I understand the Philly/Soup-nazi mentality of ordering steaks, but have the ****ing decency to look at me when you're asking me what I want! I'm sick of these guys looking away and quietly mumbling, "next", while I've been patiently waiting for them to plop down fresh meat. I understand that they deal with the tourists and the bar crowd, but treating all the customers like crap doesn't accomplish anything. Especially when they themselves are slow as **** when it comes to making the steaks. So my new rating would be 3/3.5 stars reduced to 2 because of the staff.
label: NEG

text: First of all, it's an awesome, beloved program that is very much worth supporting. Second of all, it's very easy to support delicious fried catfish. Third of all, eat the bread pudding.
label: POS

text: Have been coming here for years. This is not your Momma's diner. It serves upscale and delicious renditions of classic and fusion dishes. I love their lobster club sandwich on brioche and bucket of fries. Eggs Benedict, Omlettes, Tuna sandwich, pancakes are all great.
label: POS

text: Really NOT good. In fact, it's pretty terrible. The prices are reasonable, and the descriptions are appealing on the menu. Unfortunately, when your food arrives, it's a huge letdown. The food looks like someone else's leftovers, transferred to a clean plate. And the taste? What taste? They must have run out of that before you arrived. Find an IHOP. They, too, leave a carafe of hot coffee on your table ... that's the only positive thing going for this First Watch restaurant. Blech.
label: NEG

text: Not a big fan of Gambino's King Cake. Keep in mind I had mine shipped to PA, so they may be different if you buy locally. By the time it arrived the cake was dry and it came with the icing in a separate container and we had to ice the cake ourselves. Sure it solves the problem of the icing getting messed up, but it was odd.
label: NEG

text: City View Pizza is the best pizza I have found in North Philadelphia. By far. My boyfriend and I just moved to Philly from Miami where pizza is sorely lacking, and I was expecting to try some great pies back in the north! But to my dismay, all the other pizza joints around Temple serve cardboard-like crusts topped with sweet sauce and shredded cheese. Not delicious. Then one day, we stumbled upon City View and gave it a try. The narrow little shop is always bustling with people and the cashiers/staff are very friendly! When ordering on the phone they are efficient and never cranky. The order is always right and they save your name so when you call they can say, "Hey Shay! What'll it be tonight?" The pizza varies from night to night and sometimes is a bit skimpy on sauce, but the cheese is delicious and melted perfectly, yummy crust, and the sauce is not too sweet or bitter. Aside from pizza, CVP has great gyros and good greek salads. The fries are lacking though. Mondays are special because a large pizza is 2$ off the regular price. Each day of the week has some kind of discount. I will be a faithful CVP customer for the entirety of my residence in North Philly.
label: POS

text: My wife and I went here expecting a fantastic experience. We sat at the sushi bar in the back, which has a nice view of the restaurant. We were there on a Saturday night, and it was packed. The service was proficient, but a bit snooty. We only eat fish and veggie stuff (no shellfish, chicken, meat, etc.). Even with these restrictions, we decided to order the tasting menu as see what Morimoto could do for us. While the dry chilled sake lifted our spirits, we were underwhelmed with the food. Yeah it was good, but not $315 good for two people for dinner. Actually, not even $120 good. If you like sushi, sashimi, fantastic rolls, a cool atmosphere, great music, and awesome beer..... go to Raw on Sansom between 12th and 13th. If you want really adventurous food, with no food restrictions and a really fat wallet, then stay at Morimoto - just don't go for a sushi/sashimi night out. There are better places to go for your money.
label: NEG

text: Another cookie cutter chain sandwich shop. The sandwiches lack character. Although they are consistently wrapped, which seems more important than content, you would be better off with a grocery store deli sandwich. Skip this place.
label: NEG

text: The highlight was that the Iron Chef himself came around to the glowing table and shook our hands!!! I've never done the omakase b/c I'm too cheap but the rock shrimp tempura and the Ishi Yaki 'Buri Bop' (yellowtail) that's cooked tableside is very good.
label: POS

text: Sister's Place has always been close to my heart. I grew up a few blocks away from it. I go there about once a month for the fried chicken. They cook it fresh to order, and aside from my grandmother's, its the best I've ever had. Great prices, friendly staff, very clean place. =) Its not super fancy, but it definitely fills the 'heart warming food' bill that this city really seems to lack. They always have a ton of pies on the menu too, so if someone mentions pie, I always mention Sister's!
label: POS

text: A Monk's by any other name would taste as sweet? I'd have to squint to tell the difference in the menu and beer lists, but I think what makes Belgian Cafe interesting is that it's a neighborhood bar rather than a center city institution, and perhaps this makes more sense. I went last night and got a beer and the steak frites salad (I didn't feel like getting mussels). The meat portion was small but commiserate with the price and I didn't feel like weighing myself down anyway. It was better prepared than I actually expected. The fries were standard Monk's fries with their delicious fry sauce. I've become awfully tired of fries lately, but I just can't stop eating that sauce. Also, there was plenty of outside seating on a pretty nice day at 5:30. Note: I observed that the mussels were not served in a pot and I found this to be weird. If you must eat mussels out of a pot, be advised that you could be in for trouble.
label: POS

text: ADORE the deep dish pizza. Order a large and you'll eat for a week. It's traditional Chicago deep dish...crust cheese then sauce but that means it never gets soggy! They are super generous with toppings. The fried mushrooms are fab and the wings aren't too shabby. BTW if you refrigerate the leftovers the cheese goes so far back into the crust its like a stuffed-crust experience
label: POS

text: I have been to this location several times. Tonight we got carry out, and it served as just another reason why I enjoy going. We were in and out in 15 minutes without calling ahead. The cashiers were helpful and friendly. It wasn't too crowded, and we were able to grab a beer, watch the game, and then walk right on out with the food. I'll mention this too - The carry out bags were fully stocked with plenty of napkins, a fork for boneless wings, and two ranch sauces a piece. For my money there is nothing worse than being handed a carry out bag missing nearly everything. Definitely a good experience all around.
label: POS

text: I wanted to love the Pop Shop. As I have recently moved to Collingswood, my boyfriend and I were looking to try all the cute restaurants on Haddon Ave. Last night we spontaneously decided to go into the Pop Shop for dinner, as we passed it on our commute home and it looked rather empty, as it was only 5:30pm. We both got different kind of burgers, I built my own and he got the Cowboy Burger. Both were delicious! I love that I was able to build a burger to my taste and add a generous portion of (Maryland/Old Bay Spice) fries for a reasonable price. I do however wish I was asked how I'd like my burger cooked, as I do like my burgers a little bit on the pinker side, the one I received was VERY well done. My complaint lies in the service, although our waitress was sweet, I did feel quite hurried, which was surprising as the restaurant was empty. She approached us to take our drink order before I could even slip into the booth and take off my coat, I was caught off guard and asked what they had available, she pointed to the good ol' soda standard selection. It wasn't until I had already ordered my meal that I found out that I could have created my own flavored egg-cream soda pop, so I was immediately resentful at my plain Coca Cola. I may come back to the Pop Shop to try their grilled cheese or any time breakfast menu, but when it comes to burgers I'll take the trip into the Philly and stick to Bobby Flay's Burger Bar.
label: POS

text: So every once in awhile you have to go back do a little reflecting and eat crow. Visiting Graeber & Co, caused me to do just that. When I first moved to Boise I called them up for a mani/ pedi and was blown away by their price. Well I have since given them a shot and think I have found the salon for my mani/ pedis as well as hair. Yes, the main/ pedi is a bit higher in price than the little salons around but Graeber & Co. offer not a salon atmosphere but a spa atmosphere. The place actually reminds me of Burk Williams in LA except that I didn't see anyone running around in their white robes. As far as hair, I have tried a few different salons within the Boise area (all were fine) but I still wished my stylist in LA were here to take care of me. Now that I have Manuela I can leave a Boise salon thinking about her service and not the service I would have had if I were in LA. Manuela has 20+ years of experience, was really willing to listen and guaranteed her work...all of which are very important. The price for my hair was not really expensive at all compared to other salons in Boise. I was warned before I arrived the first time that they call people over the intercom but this didn't seem to feel intrusive. All the staff thus far have been great (nails, hair and wax are the services I have had there since) and carry the Boise personality that is so attractive.
label: POS

text: Wonderful, caring staff. They are good with grooming/baths too! Great place for dogs, they have access to a fenced in outdoors area and there are webcams so you can check in on them. Affordable prices, and very clean! They actively support animal rescue, and support local non-profits like the DE Humane Association. They even house some rescue dogs until they find their forever home. I love this place, and so does my dog! Recommend to anyone.
label: POS

text: I totally love Lithe! I was never a fitness guru. I hated exercise. Lithe has made me change my mind completely. I took my 1st class last Saturday and it was great. I got a complete workout with 2days of soreness, which is good. Lithe is truly the best exercise regimen for me. I will continue on to whip my body into shape. Thanks, Lithe!!!!!!
label: POS

text: Was there for a Saturday afternoon lunch. Only 2 other people in the restaurant, yet it took about 15 minutes for a waiter to show up. Then instead of giving us water, informed us that the kitchen was "malfunction city" so after that was fixed he'd get us drinks. Huh? Wha? I wanted to leave, but the rest of our table wanted to stay. It was then that we discovered in the menu that your first basket of chips is free, yet future baskets are $1.50?! Nice. Value the chips. The lunch menu was void for weekends, so most dishes were $10+. So now about 20 minutes later, we get our drinks and put in our order. It comes out fast, and it's fine. Nothing amazing. My dish was not worth $11. More like, $7. I also found a nice curly hair in my taco. Awesome. And a customer sitting near us had her order screwed up, but she stuck with it. Don't think I'll be going back there anytime soon. 2 stars since the food was edible.

text: Voorhees' only local coffee shop. Take it or leave it, Coffee Works has tried to update it look. With a recent renovation, the decent sized cafe does have a few areas nice for a medium group of people (5-10). I am all about local, but Coffee Works doesn't really cut it for me. The coffee isn't unique and the food tries so hard to be good but fails miserably. I would rather just go to borders or even Starbucks. At least I am getting good quality. As for music, it is typically not for a young crowd. Every time I have tried to stop by and listen to live music, Coffee Works is packed with middle aged mom's singing to the oldies. Maybe amateur night is a different story. Hopefully, Coffee Works will not have a monopoly on the "local coffee shop" business for too long, because honestly, it isn't worth it.

text: Boo bad & sloooooooooooow service. Even when a member of our group knew our waiter. The food looked overly sophisticated for how it tasted & thus was over-priced. A little bit of highway robbery here even with the high-end ingredients & the rising cost of food factored in.
