text: So I go to this IKEA once a week. I suppose, I am little bit of an "Ikea-a-holic". Everything in my apartment is from IKEA and a lot of it is over 5 years old and holding strong. Much of it is also from curb alerts, or just walking home and finding IKEA furniture outside my house. I've been going to this IKEA for years, and my favorite things are as follows: The As-Is department- like I said I go often, so I generally know what's in their catalog at any given time so much of the stuff in their AS-IS department is in perfect working order just for cheap. Hello cheap, we love you. The foodery. you can to IKEA, you're grueling through redecorating your friends place AND you didn't eat. Well IKEA has great cheap eats ranging from simple to fancy and all their hot cafeteria style food is really actually good. The delivery section will hold your furniture for you for the day for free if theirs a really cheap as is piece you want and you didn't bring your car, or your car is too small and you need to go get a zipcar truck. no problem. The rest of the store stands for itself as it is exactly like every IKEA everywhere. You find the piece of furniture you want in it's easily laid out upstairs showroom OR categorized section, you take down the location, then you go find it. If you can't find it, you ask an employee for help, it's so simple baby chimps can handle it. I usually do most of my shopping online to find what I want and then just go to pick it up. If you you have a small car and have IKEA furniture already, definitely bring an allen wrench/ hex key that way you can disassemble your as is finds and load them easier.
label: POS

text: I cannot believe I am the first person to write a review of this place! These guys are great. My family members and I have been going to them for years. They have great mechanics and great customer service. We never get nervous taking our cars in because they never find anything wrong with them and they provide fast and affordable maintenance with no surprises. An example from this week: a headlamp went out, we called and they let me bring it in a half hour before closing the same day. I pulled up and the mechanic met me at my car and replaced the bulb right then and there!!! Then I told them my brakes had been squealing, but I had a road trip planned for the next day, they order the parts that night and they then squeezed me in at opening (7am) and had me on the road at 8am!! The inspection over the summer had a note to replace brake pads next oil change, they were right. There was no pressure to do it at the time (we should have) and when we needed them to do it they did in record time! The price is always as predicted and very, very fair. It is so nice to have a car shop that you can trust and that truly wants to give you the best service at the best price and never any extras on the bill. Honest and dependable which is what I want with something as important as my car and being safe. To make a fantastic deal even better: You can always find coupons in the paper too! I do not know about all Meineke's but the one on Ridge is solid!
label: POS

text: Maybe we just ordered the wrong thing...? No, i dont think so, it was really just that bad. Besides the fact that it took almost an hour and a half to get our food (and in an empty restaurant, thats just lazy), everything was so over peppered we could barely eat it. Would not go back. We ordered: Half nachos (eh. Nothing memorable) Pork meat plate with collard greens and potato salad. This tasted like airport food. I was really craving BBQ and I have to say, this completely missed the mark. I actually have nothing positive to say about it. I don't know why this place is so popular, every time I have eaten something from here I have been sorely disappointed.
label: NEG

text: Food was delish! The hummus was very very good. The pita was a tad bit spicy, but nevertheless very good. Very attentive staff. I ordered the blackened grilled chicken, but it was a bit too spicy for me. My bad. I should have told them to go light on the spices. The fries were very good & had very good flavor. Next time, I'm going to try the onion rings, the desserts & other tasty items. For 4 people, the price was just about right.
label: POS

text: We decided to eat late lunch here on a Friday, after visiting a nearby museum. We were asked to wait at the bar for a table and probably would have waited even longer had we not taken the initiative to ask the hostess again to seat us at one of the open tables ("Oh yeah, sure, go ahead..."). I was pretty excited about this place having read all the rave reviews. We ordered some drinks and deliberated long and hard on what we wanted our burgers to look like. I opted for mushrooms & fried egg on mine, and husband asked for crab salad on his. We patiently munched on tater tots as we waited for our burgers and fries. When these hefty sandwiches finally arrived at our table, we oohed and aahed a bit before digging in. The first bite was quite tasty I'll admit, the patty nicely seasoned. Though I ordered mine medium, it came out medium rare. A couple more bites and the whole thing just started to fall apart. Before long, the burger was swimming in a pool of meat juice and egg yolk, not the most appetizing thing to look at. I didn't manage to finish mine, but I liked it well enough. I think that the main problem, though, was that we weren't blown away by any aspect of the meal. It was just... nice. I don't know if I'm comfortable shelling out close to $70 for burgers for two (with a couple of cocktails & potatoes on the side) and have it be just NICE.
label: NEG

text: I went here earlier today with my boyfriend. It was a late Sunday afternoon and not very busy. We were sat by the bartender at a table with two plates that looked like they were previously used. It took forever for our waitress (I believe her name was Alyssa) to actually come over and greet us. We ordered water, and that too took a long time to get to us. After she took our order, she did leave us chips and dip (which weren't terrible) but she forgot clean plates, silverware and napkins. She did not check on us to see if we needed refills (which we did) until our food arrived. I asked her for silverware, napkins, and refills. Five minutes later she came with silverware, and napkins but no water. She didn't apologize or anything for forgetting our water. The food we ordered (burritos) was delicious. We were done eating, and Alyssa was nowhere to be found. I would go back for food, but probably only for takeout since the service here is terrible. It is very slow, and they don't do anything to go out of their way to make you feel welcomed.
label: NEG

text: I've never really been crazy for crepes before, mainly because I so rarely have them and the ones I ate before were lackluster. Still, I was curious when i heard such good things about L'Aube, and last Saturday I decided that crepes were exactly what I needed at noontime. Was I right. I thoroughly enjoyed my strawberry and Nutella crepes, which was to be expected. My gf's omelette-eseque crepe was the game changer though. Egg, crispy bacon and goat cheese... this is what I'll get next time I'm there. Decently priced, not too filling, and just enough to handle in one sitting. The coffee was also noteworthy, coming out nice and hot and maintaining its taste to the last sip. The kicker was the owner, Jean-Luc, talking to us at length about anything that came to mind, from the layout of the city, to the American education system, to why the French don't like ketchup. You can't get that glorious type of pure Frenchness anywhere else.
label: POS

text: I was AMAZED of how AWESOME the food was. Since eating here at Taco Johns, I have yet to step foot into another Taco Bell. the food is always fresh and hot. the service is great, and their staff is very friendly. they need one in California.
label: POS

text: After reading the reviews of other Yelpers, my expectations were set pretty low for my 10 Arts dining experience. I think my low expectations were a bit too high. I made my reservations over 6 months ago, because it was Penn graduation weekend, and my parents really wanted to go there for their wedding anniversary. I called ahead, the reservationist was pleasant on the phone. Any special occasions? Yes, anniversary. Any allergies in your party? Yes, my boyfriend is of a delicate constitution. So I thought I was all set. Wrong. Disappointingly wrong. My party of 5 got there right on time, but they didn't have the "quiet booth seating" that I requested for my aging and hearing impaired parents. No, we were in the middle of the lobby, with a full view of the kitchen door. When we requested to be reseated, we were rudely told that other people had reservations and there was nothing that could be done, despite the fact that the restaurant was half empty at the time. On to the food: Prior reviewers recommended the octopus. I must say, not much about that dish was exciting. Octopus is not supposed to be rubbery, so I don't know that cooking it correctly merits any points for culinary excellence. The eggplant that came with it was mediocre. The corn chowder was a bowl of spicy, wet corn. The foie gras was fine. The server who served my poor mother her shrimp bisque spilled half of it on the table and didn't bring out a replacement bowl. Really? The entrees were even worse. I ordered the striped bass and it came out raw. I had to send it back. Not even slightly undercooked. Not sushi style tuna. Just plain raw. And the waitress didn't even take it off the bill. The waitress was also all over pushing the sides. My mother took her up on it and ordered a side of the saltiest mashed potatoes ever. I was glad they were there so at the very least, I had something to eat while I was waiting for the bass to cook. The steak frites were fine. The trout was buttery, and cooked. As an aside, I thought the portions were really big for a fine dining restaurant. Maybe if they put a little TLC into their preparation, instead of sending out half a raw fish, the experience would have been a bit better. Needless to say, we didn't stay for dessert. ERIC RIPERT, you should be ashamed.
label: NEG

text: I wonder why the wording is listed weird for this business. I'm pretty sure it's "The Basque Market" not "Basque the Market." Anyway... I'm in Boise for the week and I was wandering around downtown today killing time while B was at work. I ducked into this little shop in search of some reprieve from this relentless heat and the scorching sun (my scalp is so sunburned! it will fall off tomorrow...). It was dark and cool inside, and I was immediately greeted by a friendly man. Coolgirl was working the deli counter when I approached to look at the menu. A crisp white wine seemed like great idea so I asked about the house. Well, coolgirl gave me a sample of the house white and of the other whites they carried and discussed them with me. Very cool, hence, the title. I decided to go for the New Age White. It was very bright, clean, and easy to drink. The citrusiness (ok, so that's probably not a real word) and slight effervescence--think vinho verde--balanced out the sweetness. I got strong floral and peachy notes with a touch of honey. It was served over ice with fresh lime. Very refreshing. With cool cocktail in hand and teetering back from the brink of heatstroke, I perused the shelves of exotic basque treats. They had some interesting stuff I had not seen before (tinned octopus! and snails stewed in tomato sauce--had to get that one) and some nice Spanish wines. I wanted to pick up one of everything, but the thought of lugging around a sackful of canned goods and bottles of wine in the heat didn't appeal to me. I noticed that some of the items were past their freshness dates, which is a sad thing to see at small specialty stores. People need to buy more goodies from these places so that can stay in business! In my exhausted (been moving all weekend--packing, loading, uhauling across multiple states, unloading, reloading due to last minute apartment change at destination, and unloading again...) and dehydrated state, the wine affected me quite quickly and I got a bit chatty. Although coolgirl was trying to get some work done, she was very accommodating and nice. As I was leaving with my little parcel of goodness, she warmly welcomed me to Idaho. Sweet.
label: POS

text: Does it survive because of the cute punny name? It was understandable that Aesop's might thrive years ago, when Mass Ave was up-and-coming and had little else to offer. But it remains to this day, taking prime real estate away from restaurateurs who could do much better with this site. The taramosalata was oversalted and skimpy for what you pay; others have already bemoaned the uncomfortable chairs. Italian and Greek are among the two cuisines that are well-represented in Indy's downtown; you can no doubt find other better options in Fountain Square or south of the Wholesale District (Babe Denny).
label: NEG

text: Really great food! If you are a little hesitant to spend $$$ these days (and who isn't?), get there around 6:30 and sit at the bar. Order several appetizers and a glass of wine and see what you think. The veal potstickers are amazing, as are the lobster turnovers. Portions are reasonable and the staff is very knowledgeable. That, and their bread is simply to die for!
label: POS

text: The burger was great and I'm not even a big meat fan. I asked for medium rare and they didn't burn it. The salads are tasty, breakfasts too. The wait staff is friendly and the African bread man is nice to look at. I go to this place because it is close to my job and not as busy as the other Marathon restaurants. It's fairly priced, clean, and you can eat outside if you like. This place is just an American-cuisine spot that is not too showy yet is still part of a chain--so don't expect the most fantastic experience of your life. But it's a good place to come to for breakfast, lunch, brunch, dinner, and even come with a bar. Right in your neighborhood...if you live in Rittenhouse, that is.
label: POS

text: Pros: Convenient to Bourbon Street, rooms are decent, love that you get linen spray and eye mask, the room service staff is excellent and polite, food is pretty good. Cons: The fact that they give you earplugs is a bad sign, I was on the 8th floor and still could hear everything going on down on the street, it made getting to sleep at night difficult. So, I guess it's safe to say they arent real concerned with cleanliness.

text: Very loud, new digs on Main Street. Easy to find, less charming. Very costly but I'm sure the food is of high quality. Service may very depending on attitude of server. Nice local place in Downtown Safety Harbor, hard to get the bill for a motorcycle joint.

text: Excellent authentic Mexican cuisine. Atmosphere is cozy and the service is fast. This is not a big restaurant, but there is a take out service available. I've had the enchilada dinner multiple times and enjoyed it. The food is cooked well and presentation is surprising for such a small restaurant. The taste and authenticity far exceeds the quality of similar restaurants in the area, even more expensive restaurants. The quantity of food is also great. There are about two portion sizes of food per entree. Prices range from $8 to $20 per entree.

text: I know this is the place to go for any kind of cupcake you'd ever want, but the place itself is so interesting and pretty! Walking into the shop, I loved the display cases, they are amazing vintage pieces instead of the average glass cases. Adorable decor. If Hello Kitty owned a business, this is what it would look like. One of the other reviews calls this a 'hipster city-folk fad' but as a very dorky mom, I felt at home and I plan on taking my daughter here for her birthday. Who doesn't love a cute bakery with equally delicious goods?

text: Staying nearby on Christmas, so we were worried we would have granola bars for dinner. Instead, we found Sage open and inviting. The staff was super-friendly and the food was very good! We recommend it to everyone!

text: A complete rip-off. I've been to tapas places in many cities and this is among the worst. Apamate is the only place I've been to in many years where we actually had to go have ANOTHER dinner after we ate there! And my girlfriend doesn't even eat very much...

Your best bet is in the outerwear and men's suits. $38 for a beautiful worsted wool coat? Now that's more like it. Still, I walked out with nothing.

text: Ah, New Jersey. The state of "liberty and prosperity." Liberty: their liquor stores are free from the the tyrannical grasp of state-controlled liquor laws. Meaning: prices are cheaper, employees are helpful and, gasp, cheerful. Prosperity: Me taking advantage of their Thanksgiving hours while Philadelphia's liquor stores decided turkey and family was more important. I came across three different employees eager to help me find the best wine selection. After politely dismissing the first two, I finally obliged the next fellow. He lead me to a lovely selection of bottles, all falling within my price range, and now, as I relax on my couch, swirling my glass of 9 dollar Tempranillo, I'm happy I went to Canal's.
